MACCALLUM: So the serial criminal, this guy that you see being walked in here, you know what he is accused of, of course, suspected of ramming his car, weaving it back and forth to hit as many people as possible, in a Christmas parade in Wisconsin. He's now facing a sixth homicide charge following the death of this little boy, little baseball player, eight-year- old Jackson Sparks who was remembered by the members of his team. Jackson died of a "cranial cerebral injury and blunt force trauma." But some people who cover stories out there don't think that this story is really worth covering all that much. So why is that? Pete Hegseth is up next. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) MACCALLUM: So the suspect in the Wisconsin Christmas parade tragedy now faces a sixth count of intentional homicide after eight-year-old Jackson Sparks. This little boy on the left side of your screen died of his injuries. He was marching with his baseball team in the parade that evening when the driver crashed his SUV into all of the people who were walking through that parade that night. Now, the suspect, Darrell Brooks, was reportedly considered high risk before he got out on $1,000 in bail. The mother of one of his kids said she wished she hadn't bailed him out. He was in court on more charges today of assault as well. Fox and Friends co-host Pete Hegseth is going to join us in just a moment, but first to correspondent Griff Jenkins who's reporting on the very latest in this awful tragic story from Washington DC. Hi, Griff. GRIFF JENKINS, FOX NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Martha. We're learning a lot more about this suspect, 39-year-old Darrell Brooks who was in court today on charges unrelated to last Sunday's parade attack. And during the hearing today where Brooks faces five counts, including two felonies of bail jumping and second degree recklessly endangering safety, his attorney Joe Domask withdrew from the case telling the court relationships and familiarities between the attorney and the communities affected by instance arising in the Waukesha County holiday parade have created a concurrent conflict of interest. The judge granted the motion. Now, today's charges stem from Brooks' allegedly running over the mother of his child in early November with the same red SUV used to plow through that Christmas parade. We're also learning, Martha, that in this case Brooks was deemed a high risk by a pretrial assessment investigator following his November 5th arrest, leading officials worried he would commit another crime. Yet, he was still given a low $1,000 bail, which he posted days later. This comes as prosecutors charged Brooks with that six counts of first degree intentional homicide in the parade attack following the death of eight-year-old Jackson Sparks as you mentioned, who was walking alongside his 12-year-old brother, Tucker, who was also injured. In all, six people were killed, more than 60 were injured. And, Martha, it's hard to overstate just how lengthy Brooks' rap sheet really is. His criminal record dates back to 1999 when he pleaded guilty to felony battery. He's also a registered sex offender in Nevada after impregnating a 15-year-old girl, and he has an active warrant for his arrest there for another sex crime charged. Now, he's currently being held on a $5 million bail in the parade attack. And he will make a court appearance in that case until after the New Year, although we will see him again on December 20th in court, in a hearing set to appoint a public defender and today's charges. Martha. MACCALLUM: Griff, thank you very much. Fox and Friends Weekend co-host Pete Hegseth joins me now. Pete, I can't help but think if they had slapped a $5 million bail on him after one of those prior offenses, molesting a child, all of those prior offenses. These people whose pictures that we keep putting on the screen, and this little boy, would be alive today. PETE HEGSETH, FOX NEWS HOST: Absolutely. He shouldn't even have a $5 million bill today. Why is their bill set at all? And when you look at those pictures where you were talking that picture on the left, Jackson Sparks, that is the picture, and all of all of those people their pure innocence, pure innocence taken away by pure evil. And the reason why this is treated so differently is because of politics, is because of narrative. And in this particular case, you had district attorneys with very particular views about what's wrong with our society and it's usually siding on the side of criminals. It wasn't just him running over his girlfriend, there was a prior attack six months earlier as well in Georgia, where he was charged with misdemeanor abuse for beating that very same woman there, shot a firearm at his cousin outside of his house. I mean, it's a 20-year record. They risk, they deemed him high at risk. This is an attack that was entirely preventable based entirely on a philosophy that sides with criminals. MACCALLUM: It's just so insane and it lacks any common sense what kind of judge, what kind of attorney looks at this case and doesn't figure out this is not going to be reformed. This person is not going to be reformed. He has broken his social contract time and time, and time again. So where are these people's brains? Where are their heads? You know, I understand people who want to do reform, who want to make sure that people get equal time, you know, depending on your economic status, I get that. This is horrible. People should pay for having passed this over and allow this man to be free. HEGSETH: Absolutely they should. Ideology, often clouds judgment and common sense in this particular case -- MACCALLUM: Or laziness I think in some cases -- HEGSETH: Or laziness. MACCALLUM: Like what he did? HEGSETH: Or rushing things through or using COVID as an excuse to say we're not going to detain people anymore who are at risk. Any number of reasons are unacceptable. That's why you saw John Chisholm, the DA, come out say we made a mistake here, except he's been saying for over a decade his philosophy is. And he knew and he's admitted that it would lead to people getting killed at some point. And here it did, right? MACCALLUM: I want to play this quickly. This is Peter Doocy and Jen Psaki. Watch this. I want to get quick thought, Pete, on the other side. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) PETER DOOCY, FOX NEWS WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Why hasn't the President visited the members of this Christmas parade attack? JEN PSAKI, WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY: Obviously, any President going to visit a community requires a lot of assets requires taking their resources. And it's not something that I have -- a trip previewed at this point in time, but we remain in touch with local officials and certainly our hearts are with the community as they've gone through such a difficult time. (END VIDEO CLIP) MACCALLUM: Well, that's comforting. Why do you think that is? HEGSETH: Wrong narrative, wrong narrative, wrong perpetrator and wrong motives. And in any particular case, they're looking at something that advances their narrative. In this particular case, Darrell Brooks, no one's talked about what -- they've talked a lot about his rap sheet, what about his ideological background? What about the fact that he's member of militant black organizations that believed in killing Jews blatantly anti- Semitic, blatantly anti-white people. They don't want to talk about those things, they want to talk about an SUV as if a vehicle did it in this particular case. And it's pretty tough to look families in the eye when you're a part of a party that's been willing to enable defunding the police and softening sentences for criminals. So they're flying right to Minnesota, I'm from there, it's not far. MACCALLUM: Yes. Yes, as Greg Gutfeld said you can run over a Christmas parade and kill twice as many people as the Boston Marathon bombers and they will call it an accident. Many in the media said that the car did this. This guy is the suspect not the car. Pete, thank you. It's always good to have you with us. HEGSETH: Thank you. MACCALLUM: Thanks for sticking around tonight, appreciate it. So that is THE STORY of Tuesday, November the 30th, last day of November. THE STORY goes on. headline: DATELINE for September 9, 2022, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [22:00:15] LESTER HOLT, NBC DATELINE HOST: I`m Lester Holt. Tonight on Dateline, a dramatic new development in the story of a wife, a mistress, and maybe a murderer. BONNIE CONTRERAS, BILL HALL`S MISTRESS: How many more bombshells is there going to be? F. HALL: She goes, I`m having an affair with your husband. ANDREA CANNING, NBC DATELINE CORRESPONDENT: You`re getting text messages from Bonnie of the two of them having sex. CONTRERAS: She saw me and then made the U turn. I looked in my rearview mirror and it was Frances. F. HALL: I get her little finger. CANNING (on camera): The middle finger? F. HALL: Right. I start following her. CONTRERAS: I said, what the hell. F. HALL: She brakes. And I brake and I forgot to stop. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: He`s pronounced dead at the hospital. F. HALL: I lost my husband, the man that I love. TIMOTHY LOVETT, PROSECUTION COLLISION EXPERT: This is not an accident. SCOTT SIMPSON, PROSECUTOR: She doesn`t stop the vehicle. If it`s an accident, you stop your vehicle. F. HALL: I did not deliberately hurt him. CANNING (on camera): A lot of hatred and anger in this case. NICO LAHOOD, CRIMINAL DISTRICT ATTORNEY: A lot. LEIGH CUTTER, FRANCES HALL`S ATTORNEY: To see manipulation, you have all the elements. NIKKI HALL, BILL HALL`S DAUGHTER: Her story changed, I don`t know how many times. CANNING (on camera): How do we know who to believe? CONTRERAS: That`s the world`s decision. HOLT (voice-over): Here`s Andrea Canning with "Collision." CANNING (voice-over): This is the story of two intense women battling for the heart of one much loved man. It`s about sex, secrets, and lies, red hot Texas passion and a bitter feud, all leading to a final showdown on a two lane highway. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Bexar County 911. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: I got a black Escalade and a Range Rover. They`re hauling ass, acting like idiots. CANNING (voice-over): A high speed chase that went horribly, horribly wrong. N. HALL: It was a nightmare. CANNING (voice-over): When the dust settled, one life would be over. Many others shattered. HANK HALL, BILL HALL`S COUSIN: We all lost here. CANNING (voice-over): And tonight, there`s a Hall new chapter. San Antonio, Texas, home of the Alamo, The Riverwalk, and the Hall family. Three generations of truckers with deep roots in the city. It was here that Bill Hall met the love of his life at the tender age of 16. Her name was Frances. (on camera): What happened the first time you laid eyes on Bill? F. HALL: I just fell in love with him. I knew this was the man I was going to marry. CANNING: At 16? F. HALL: At 16. CANNING (voice-over): They married right out of high school. A year later, daughter Nikki was born. (on camera): Where your parents in love? N. HALL: Oh yes. We definitely saw love growing up in the house. F. HALL: I love my baby. CANNING (voice-over): For years after Nikki came Justin. Bill worked hard to give his young family a better life. F. HALL: Bill used to clean airplanes. He went to college. And on the weekends if he was off, he`d go dig ditches. We made ends meet. CANNING (voice-over): But his true passion was big rigs. So one day he up and quit school started his own business, Bill Hall Jr. Trucking. F. HALL: That`s what his family did for a living so it`s in their blood. CANNING (voice-over): Bill got his first truck and went to work delivering topsoil, while Frances hit the phones to drum up new business. F. HALL: He was a dreamer. And he always said I`m going to go big vieja. Vieja is a Hispanic term, which means old lady. CANNING (voice-over): After just a few years, Bill and Frances turned that one truck into a fleet of 130. At its height, their empire was valued at more than $15 million. (on camera): All his dreaming paid off. F. HALL: And hard work. He put his life his heart and soul into it. Bill was Bill Hall Jr. Trucking. CANNING (voice-over): But for Bill, it wasn`t all work and no play. N. HALL: He was a daredevil. He loved racing. And in his later years he loved hunting. He was a man`s man. CANNING (voice-over): And also a bit of a ladies man according to Bill`s cousin Hank. H. HALL: You know beautiful women. You work hard, you play hard, and you do things, you know, that you`re not supposed to be doing. He was a great man but he was not the perfect man. CANNING (voice-over): Bill`s imperfections became painfully clear nearly 32 years into their marriage when Frances says she got a call from a mysterious woman. It was September 13th, 2013, Friday the 13th. [22:05:14] F. HALL: She goes, you don`t know me but I`m having an affair with your husband. CANNING (on camera): Wow. F. HALL: I was in shock. CANNING (voice-over): Heartbroken, furious. Frances says she confronted Bill and asked, was it true? F. HALL: By that time he is crying, and telling me that he`s sorry? That it`s true. I was devastated. CANNING (on camera): This is three decades of marriage. F. HALL: And I finally asked him, how long has this been going on? He cried again. Told me, three years. And I go, this is not an affair, this is a relationship. CANNING (voice-over): About that and only that she and the other woman agreed. (on camera): You don`t like the word mistress, do you? CONTRERAS: No, I don`t. CANNING (voice-over): This is Bonnie Contreras. (on camera): What is it about that word that bothers you? CONTRERAS: Mistress, it just sounds like I don`t want to say, yes, that I was the side person because I was more than that to him. This man was the man I wanted to marry and spend the rest of my life with. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie was a 28-year-old single mom when they met, about 20 years younger than Bill and Frances. She said their love affair bloomed in the most unlikely of places. CONTRERAS: I met him at a Spinach Festival. CANNING (on camera): Spinach? CONTRERAS: Spinach Festival, I was helping my aunt sell chicken on a stick, believe it or not. I know it sounds kind of corny, but that`s how I met him. CANNING (voice-over): Bill happened to stroll by that chicken stand with some friends. CONTRERAS: As soon as I saw Bill, we kind of just locked eyes. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie was intrigued enough by this handsome older gentleman to sneak a peek at his ring finger. CONTRERAS: No wedding ring. No, no mark. You know, I figured single. CANNING (voice-over): According to Bonnie, the two started to spend nearly every day together. CONTRERAS: I fell in love with him. I didn`t expect it. It`s not something that I was looking for at all. I love my Bill. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie said Bill told her he was separated from his wife and going through a divorce. CONTRERAS: And I took his word, I never again bothered him about it. CANNING (voice-over): He affectionately called her his Gorda, his chubby lady. And during their three years together, Bill lavished Bonnie with attention, spa days, vacations, and even breast implants. CONTRERAS: I wasn`t that big. I was maybe a small beam. And he goes go dome, we`ll pay for them. CANNING (voice-over): And then she says a five carat diamond ring. CONTRERAS: It meant love, it meant friendship, it meant a future together. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie denies calling Frances out of the blue. She says Frances had known about the relationship for years. And that the two women even spoke by phone about the financial arrangements of a divorce. CONTRERAS: Who was going to keep what and, you know, she was just going on and on about the properties and about money, about the company. And I said I`m not even asking for none of that stuff. I don`t want none of it. CANNING (voice-over): Whichever version was true, the two women had never met because Hank told Bill he needed to break it off with Bonnie before something bad happened. H. HALL: I said you need to get out of that relationship. Don`t turn back. CANNING (on camera): Did you kind of feel like, hey, Bill, you`re playing with fire and -- H. HALL: It`s exactly what I told him. I said he needed to go fix this man. You know, fix your house. Frances threw him out. He went back to Bonnie and he would go back to begging Frances to go back. He`s very confused. I`ve never seen Bill like that, never in my life. CANNING (voice-over): Frances was conflicted too, take Bill back or kick him out for good. The morning of October 9th, her anger boiled over. F. HALL: He was brushing his teeth. And I glanced over and I just -- I was enraged. CANNING (voice-over): She started pulling his hair, tousled with him all around the house. Bill appeared to take the assault as a joke. F. HALL: He was doing these little dances, he does. And it upset me so much and I kicked him in he goes, stop already. I go, no. CANNING (voice-over): She went after his prized possessions, knocking over his custom Harley Davidson and hitting their new Range Rover with a stick. F. HALL: He pushed me down. I fell down. And he took off and waved at him, smiling. CANNING (voice-over): The following day was rough for Frances. Her family coaxed her out of the house to watch her niece`s volleyball game. Then on her way home, driving her Cadillac Escalade. F. HALL: And Bill in his bike. And back of Bill, I see the Range Rover. And I`m like, who is that? CANNING (voice-over): The vehicles were coming toward her in the opposite lane. And as they passed, Frances did a double take. Sitting behind the wheel of her family`s brand new Range Rover was Bill`s mistress, Bonnie Contreras. Frances said they locked eyes for the first time. F. HALL: And of course, I get her little finger. [22:10:02] CANNING (on camera): Like the middle finger? F. HALL: Right. And I keep going. CANNING (voice-over): Furious she called her daughter Nikki. N. HALL: She said I`m turning around I`m going to confront her. CANNING (voice-over): What did you say to your mom? N. HALL: I said, good. Just being careful. CANNING (voice-over): Not likely. All hell was about to break loose. HOLT (voice-over): When we come back. (on camera): Frances follows through on her threat. F. HALL: I make the biggest choice of my life. I pulled over. And I turned around. HOLT (voice-over): Moments later, horror. F. HALL: She breaks and I break. And I forgot to stop. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) CANNING (voice-over): October 10th, 2013, here on this stretch of San Antonio highway, two women vying for one man spotted each other for the first time, Frances, the wife, and Bonnie, the mistress. F. HALL: I make the biggest choice of my life. I pulled over and I turned around. CANNING (voice-over): Turned around to chase down her romantic rival. (on camera): How fast are you going? F. HALL: I`m doing about 65, 70. She`s in a super sport Range Rover. This thing will go fast, my Range Rover. [22:15:00] CANNING (voice-over): Frances stepped on the gas and soon had Bonnie in her sights. F. HALL: I`m asking her to pull over. She tell no, pull over and nope. But she kept playing this cat and mouse and she kept breaking. CANNING (voice-over): She said Bonnie repeatedly slammed on the brakes, forcing Frances to slam on hers. Frances had a large slab of granite in the back of her Escalade from a home renovation project. F. HALL: So I can hear this piece of granite every time I break because it moves. CANNING (voice-over): As Bonnie accelerated, Frances stayed on her. It was as if she had developed tunnel vision, could focus on only one thing. F. HALL: I`m going to confront her. I`m done. I`ve had it with her. I`m going to tell her, you want him, keep him. CANNING (voice-over): The him in all of this, Bill, had been riding his motorcycle in front of Bonnie. But as the chase unfolded, he suddenly slowed down. F. HALL: All this time Bill is in front of us. And I see Bill pulling over and she`s passing him. CANNING (voice-over): Then Frances said, Bill dropped back to her right. F. HALL: And I`m passing Bill. I see Bill from my passenger window, and she breaks and I brake, and I heard something, and I forgot to stop. CANNING (voice-over): That piece of granite again, Frances thought. And she continued to chase after Bonnie still hell bent on confronting her. Suddenly Bonnie made a U turn. And as she makes a U turn. I make a U turn. She takes off. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: I got a black Escalade and a black Range Rover. They`re traveling at a high rate of speed, I don`t know, 90, 100 miles an hour -- that black Range Rover was. CANNING (voice-over): An off duty officer spotted Bonnie and Frances and called it in. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: They`re hauling ass -- driving on the wrong side of the road, acting like idiots. CANNING (voice-over): Frances was still on Bonnie`s tail when -- F. HALL: I hear this wind coming in. CANNING (voice-over): The howl of the wind snapped Frances out of her trance. She looked back and realized her third row passenger window was shattered. And then she realized something else. She couldn`t see Bill anywhere. Frances called her sister Connie who lived close by then she called her daughter Nikki. N. HALL: She goes I can`t find your dad. I don`t know where your dad is. I`m turning around. CANNING (voice-over): Frances started to make her way back down the highway. She spoke to Connie again. F. HALL: My sister tells me I found him. CANNING (voice-over): Connie had jumped in her own car and soon came upon Bill and his bike by the side of the road. He`d crashed and was in bad shape. Police were already at the scene when Frances arrived. F. HALL: And into some running to him, an officer grabs me and they yank him. I heard somebody yelled, that`s his wife leave her alone. And I get down to where he`s at. And he`s alive. CANNING (on camera): Do you say anything to him? F. HALL: I was just in shock. And he kept telling me, I can`t breathe. And I told him calm down, dad. Calm down. CANNING (voice-over): Bill had internal injuries. Whatever happened, the wreck was so severe that even knocked his boots off. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Sierra-4, here comes your bird. CANNING (voice-over): They took him away in the helicopter? F. HALL: They got a gurney and he grabbed my arm, and he goes, vieja, come with me. I go, I`m coming dad. And they take him and I remember he told them, she needs to come with me. CANNING (voice-over): But officers wouldn`t allow Frances in the chopper, wouldn`t allow her to go anywhere in fact. F. HALL: And I told the officer, I`m his wife, and he said turn around and he handcuffed me, put in the back, and they`ve left with Bill. CANNING (voice-over): It was only then, Frances says, that it all came together in her mind. The thump, the broken window, somehow Bill`s bike and her Escalade must have collided. (on camera): I think some people might find it hard to believe that you wouldn`t realize that you had hit a motorbike. F. HALL: I didn`t feel anything. I heard a thump. I thought it was this piece of granite. CANNING (voice-over): Police detained her for questioning while Bill`s family took up a vigil at the hospital. N. HALL: When they told us that he had passed away, it was just complete shock. H. HALL: I kind of screamed out and, you know, I just couldn`t believe it. I didn`t want to believe it. CANNING (voice-over): Frances was still in the back of the patrol car when she got the news. F. HALL: I noticed three people come to me wearing suits. And one of them tells me that he hadn`t made it. And I was like, you`re full of it. I go, no, he did. I go, just go check. They come back until we Ms. Hall`s husband didn`t make hit. CANNING (voice-over): With Bill dead, Frances was not only a grieving widow. She was now clearly a suspect. Police took her to the station for questioning. And she wasn`t ready to answer anything. [22:20:03] F. HALL: I need my attorney. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: OK. I completely understand. OK. F. HALL: I`m terrified. CANNING (voice-over): Frances appeared to be in denial. F. HALL: Bill, please. Bill, come back. CANNING (voice-over): But if Frances wasn`t talking to the police, the other woman in Bill`s life was. And she said Bill`s death was no accident. HOLT (voice-over): Coming up, Bonnie story, terrifying. CONTRERAS: I`m driving and I feel somebody hit me from behind. HOLT (voice-over): What she says Frances was really up to on that highway. CONTRERAS: I just slid out big old scream. HOLT (voice-over): When Dateline continues. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) CANNING (voice-over): On his last day on earth, Bill Hall was staying with girlfriend Bonnie Contreras. The two had plans to pick up Bill`s motorcycle at a storage facility for a bike rally they`d attend the next day. CONTRERAS: And he was laying in our bed, taking a nap. And that was two hours before he died. I woke them up and I said, hon, it`s getting late. I said we got to go pick up the bike before it gets dark. [22:25:05] CANNING (voice-over): And that Bonnie said is how she and Bill ended up on the road that fateful evening, with Bonnie behind the wheel of the Range Rover, Bill in front of her on his baby blue motorcycle. Neither of them knowing that Frances quite by chance, was coming from the opposite direction. But Bonnie`s version of events would differ sharply from the tale Frances told. CONTRERAS: He`s driving, I`m driving. Somewhere along the way, we stopped at a light and he pulled up beside me in the other lane. He tells me, I love you so much, Gorda. He`s like, I`m so happy. And that was the last time I heard his voice. CANNING (voice-over): The light turned green, and everything changed. CONTRERAS: He was in front of me and I`m driving and I feel somebody hit me from behind. At first I thought it was an accident. CANNING (voice-over): A sudden jolt, then another. CONTRERAS: I feel another hit. And I said, what the hell. And I looked in my rearview mirror and it was Frances. CANNING (voice-over): Bill`s wife, they`d spoken by phone but never met. Bonnie said she never saw Frances on the road before she felt those jolts, never taunted her with her middle finger as Frances claimed. Now, Bonnie said Frances wasn`t just chasing her. She was actually repeatedly ramming her Cadillac Escalade into the back of the Range Rover. CONTRERAS: I started screaming because she wouldn`t stop hitting me. She kept ramming her vehicle into me. CANNING (voice-over): She said, France`s story that Bonnie kept slamming on your brakes was nonsense. (on camera): You are accused of -- CONTRERAS: Brake checking her, brake checking her. No, I was trying to get away from that woman. So I started speeding up, as she kept ramming me from behind, and she threw me onto oncoming traffic. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie said she was hit so hard, her purse fell off the front seat. CONTRERAS: Right and my stuff flew to the floor. CANNING (voice-over): And here another significant difference from Frances`s version. Bonnie says that when she swerved back into her lane, she looked in her rearview mirror and saw Bill was now riding behind her between the two SUVs. CONTRERAS: And I see her coming up behind Bill and I`m yelling at the top of my lungs, and I see her hit Bill and I see Bill fly and then I see the bike fly. CANNING (voice-over): According to Bonnie, she saw Frances deliberately hit Bill from behind, then keep chasing her. CONTRERAS: I was shaking and I was in shock. I didn`t understand why she hadn`t stopped when she hit Bill. I couldn`t understand it. I still don`t understand it. I felt like stopping but I didn`t know if she had a gun. In my first instinct is to make a quick U turn. (on camera): So she does a U turn too? CONTRERAS: Yes, she`s right behind me. She continues to hit me. And we`ve been passed the scene of her, Bill is clinging to his life. And even at that she didn`t bother to stop hitting me. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie eventually made her way back to where Bill lay by the road. CONTRERAS: And I see just hecticness everywhere, police cars, detectives, ambulance. CANNING (voice-over): She said she tried to get to Bill but the officers wouldn`t let her near him. CONTRERAS: No, I wanted to hug him. I wanted to hug him. I wanted to tell him everything will be OK. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie watch the helicopter take Bill away. Hours later, a police officer gave her the news she was dreading. CONTRERAS: He goes, Bill has passed away. And I just slid out big old scream. CANNING (voice-over): So there was Bonnie`s version. This was no accident. Frances purposely ramped her repeatedly and fatally knocked Bill off the road. (on camera): Is there only one person to blame for this in your eyes? CONTRERAS: Of course, it`s Frances. She started that high speed chase. She chose to turn around. Why? You know you`re going to cause some sort of trouble. CANNING (voice-over): And when investigators looked at the evidence and heard Bonnie`s version of events, they came to the same conclusion. Nico LaHood was the District Attorney of San Antonio. LAHOOD: The bottom line for us was this, objectively we do not support this behavior. CANNING (voice-over): Frances was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon for chasing after Bonnie and for the death of her husband, Bill Hall Jr. She was charged with murder. LAHOOD: We felt that there was an attempt and an aggravated assault and in that process, a life was lost, which gets felony murder. CANNING (voice-over): But Frances said the real aggressor was Bonnie and she said she had proof. HOLT (voice-over): Coming up, Frances says Bill told her that Bonnie was obsessed with him, but that he wanted out. [22:29:55] F. HALL: He goes I can`t get rid of this person. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) CANNING (voice-over): Frances Hall was out on bail, facing a murder charge for the high speed chase that ended with the death of her husband, Bill. The key witness against her, Bill`s mistress, Bonnie Contreras. But according to Frances and her daughter, if anyone should be blamed for what happened, it was Bonnie. N. HALL: She has a lot of responsibility or full responsibility in causing this. She ruined a family. CANNING (voice-over): The way the Hall family tells it. Bonnie was a gold digger, a stalker and a liar who had been manipulating and threatening Bill for years. Frances said that after she learned about the affair, she learned the truth about Bonnie from Bill himself. F. HALL: He laid it all out. He said I am going to tell you everything, vieja. CANNING (voice-over): The family insists Bonnie told Frances about the affair because she was angry over all things, a manicure. N. HALL: She was upset because my father wouldn`t give her $100 to get her nails done. CANNING (voice-over): They said Bill told them that Bonnie had been stalking their Hall family on Facebook . [22:35:05] N. HALL: She had created a fake account with a fake profile picture and friend requested the entire family. Everyone accept it. My mom had her. I had her aunts, uncles, cousins. CANNING (voice-over): The family said Bill told them that`s how Bonnie gathered information that she would use to manipulate him. N. HALL: If we went on a trip as a family or if he took my mother to Las Vegas immediately after he would have to take her somewhere. CANNING (voice-over): According to Frances and Nikki, Bill said he wanted to break up with Bonnie. But she threatened to air their affair all over the internet. F. HALL: He goes, I can`t get rid of this person. She had over 2,000 pictures. In my 34 years of knowing Bill, I don`t have that many pictures. Who does that? CANNING (voice-over): Frances said Bill told her, Bonnie also stalked her and her family. F. HALL: She knew where my kids lived. She knew my schedule. He said that I would go to my grocery store. And she`d be there following me. CANNING (voice-over): Even said the Halls followed her and Bill into a movie theater. N. HALL: Bonnie track them and was sitting three rows behind them. She was kind of like a fatal attraction just or cycle. CANNING (on camera): She claimed that she was in love with Bill, that he was going to leave you, they were going to start a family, they were going to be married. F. HALL: She got an abortion. Tell me if she was starting with them. She got an abortion. CANNING (voice-over): Bill wanted Bonnie to have an abortion, said Frances. But Bonnie wouldn`t do it unless Bill gave her something in return. F. HALL: The only way she`d get an abortion if you bought her breast implants. Which she did, she got rid of the baby. N. HALL: I despise her. And she has not stopped embarrassing our family. It`s like can you just go away? Can you just leave us alone, go find another married man because this is what she does for a living. She strips or she gets with married men. CANNING (voice-over): In the end said the Halls, Bonnie told Frances about the affair as a final act of desperation, an attempt to hold on to Bill who was about to drop her. F. HALL: I think she finally thought, hey, I`m losing this man. I`m losing my bread and butter here, her sugar daddy. This girl was not in love with Bill. I don`t even think she knows what the word love means. CANNING (voice-over): Of course, Bonnie sees things very differently. (on camera): They`ve really gone after you with names. CONTRERAS: Of course. And I understand where the Halls are coming from. It`s a pretty big pill to swallow when your husband wants to divorce you after 32 years, you know, and of course they`re never going to say anything good about me. CANNING: Do you want to clear it up, were you an exotic dancer? CONTRERAS: I worked at a strip club. Yes. And that was way before. CANNING: As a dancer? CONTRERAS: Yes. And that was a mistake that, I mean, I regret that, no one is perfect. CANNING (voice-over): But the fake Facebook accounts stalking Frances, the abortion in exchange for breast implants. None of that ever happened, said Bonnie. CONTRERAS: For her to sit there and say that I switched a baby`s life that was going inside of me coming from a man that I love dearly for breast augmentation, ridiculousness. CANNING (voice-over): Each woman clung to her truth. The battle for Bill raged. H. HALL: He couldn`t stop Bonnie and really couldn`t stop Frances really, you know. CANNING (on camera): It sounds like two hurricanes. H. HALL: Oh, yes. CANNING (voice-over): Then about a week before Bill`s death, the hurricanes collided. Not on the road. Not yet. This war was waged via text. (on camera): You`re getting text messages from Bonnie of the two of them having sex. F. HALL: Uh-huh. HOLT (voice-over): Coming up, the case heads to court where one expert testifies that Frances deliberately rammed Bonnie. LOVETT: This is not an accident. HOLT (voice-over): While another expert provides a demonstration that seems to show the SUVs never even touched. CHARLES RUBLE, ACCIDENT RECONSTRUCTIONIST: That simple physics. [22:38:57] HOLT (voice-over): When Dateline continues. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) CANNING (voice-over): The battle over Bill Hall Jr. had gone on for weeks. And it all led up to a confrontation about a week before his death. Bill and Frances met at this hotel. She said they were trying to work things out. But then Bonnie showed up at the front desk. N. HALL: Saying she was his wife and she needed to get access to his room and my dad told them, no, she`s not my wife. My wife is here with me. CANNING (voice-over): Security asked Bonnie to leave though she insists she never claimed to be Bill`s wife. But all parties agree that night an all- out war began via text. (on camera): You`re getting text messages from Bonnie of the two of them having sex. F. HALL: Pictures of sexual positions. CANNING (voice-over): Photos with captions like, this is what he really likes you fat old woman. (on camera): Normally the mistress keeps a very low profile. F. HALL: She wanted to make sure I knew now she was in the picture. CANNING (voice-over): Did she ever? Many of the messages are too graphic to show. But you can get a good sense of them from these excerpts. Let me know if you want some good juicy pics of me and your hubby, you stupid old person, keep fixing yourself up maybe he`ll find you more attractive. (on camera): What`s the worst text message she sent you? F. HALL: The hollow bitch. CANNING: She actually called you -- F. HALL: Hollow. CANNING: Because? F. HALL: Of my hysterectomy. CANNING (voice-over): Complete with a diagram to reinforce the point. Bonnie admits she sent those nasty texts. (on camera): You have to imagine though that people are going to see this and they`re going to think that some of those text messages are cruel. CONTRERAS: I never sent her pictures of me and Bill having sexual intercourse. What I did send her pictures of was three butt pics of me. And that`s because she infuriated me because she told me that my butt looked like a broken saddlebag. It looked like a broken toilet seat. Trust me. She was going at me very hard. CANNING (voice-over): In fact, Bonnie, says it was Frances who started the text war. CONTRERAS: Plain and simple, I was defending myself. CANNING (on camera): The texts that Frances said hurt her the most was the one where you called her hollow and sent the diagram of a woman who had had a hysterectomy. CONTRERAS: That is cruel. CANNING: That would hit a woman hard. CONTRERAS: And I`m not happy about that. CANNING: Why did you do it? CONTRERAS: Because I was pissed at her. She was telling me vicious ugly thing. [22:45:00] CANNING: Did you send any back to her that were nasty as well not really, no, because it`d be hard not to engage. F. HALL: Well, yes, I started to at the hotel, but I think I did one or two. CANNING (voice-over): Had them in the palm of your hand and couldn`t keep him. Frances wrote to Bonnie, keep sending fatal attraction. Cops need all the pics. F. HALL: I mean, I couldn`t keep up, I text slow. This girl`s young. She knows technology. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie says Frances more than held her own. Don`t flatter yourself. He`s been cheating on you with me. But says Frances, the nastier text, Bonnie, received didn`t come from her. She says Bill sent them. F. HALL: Bill grabbed the phone and he said let me take care of her. CONTRERAS: No, he didn`t. That was her. It was her sending those text messages. Bill wouldn`t have never disrespected me like that. CANNING (voice-over): But if there was any doubt that she`d been following the Halls, she seemed to confirm it herself by sending photos of their house and Frances`s car. (on camera): Why were you sending those pictures? CONTRERAS: To piss her off. To defend myself. CANNING: Why, what are you -- I mean, you`re the one -- CONTRERAS: Her telling me that bill didn`t love me, her telling me that Bill was using me. CANNING: But Bonnie, you`re the one who`s having the affair with Bill. So why are you attacking his wife? CONTRERAS: Because she was attacking me and I will defend myself. CANNING (voice-over): One week after that text message viewed came the car chase that left Bill Hall dead. Nearly three years after that, Frances Hall went on trial for murder. Prosecutors Stephanie Paulissen and Scott Simpson laid out the case for the jury. STEPHANIE PAULISSEN, PROSECUTOR: We understand why she was angry. But that`s not justification to go attempt to run down your husband`s mistress and kill him in the process. CANNING (voice-over): The star witness for the prosecution, Bonnie Contreras. CONTRERAS: I start to get hit from behind. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie told the jury how she watched with horror as she believed Frances deliberately knocked Bill off the road. CONTRERAS: -- can fly off the motorcycle. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie said she later discovered Frances`s daughter Nikki Hall had left a message on her voicemail during the car chase, a message that seemed to speak to Frances`s intent that evening. N. HALL: I told you to watch your back, you -- stupid slut. CONTRERAS: What does that tell you? That they were out to cause harm to somebody. LOVETT: This is not an accident. CANNING (voice-over): Tim Lovett was the state`s collision reconstruction expert. He said the evidence showed Frances chased and hit Bonnie. LOVETT: That Escalade definitely hit that Range Rover at least two maybe three times. But Frances`s defense attorneys, Leigh Cutter and Jean Brown said investigators made a big mistake when they bought into the story of Bonnie Contreras. CUTTER: Everyone got their information from one person at the scene. That`s Bonnie and Bonnie lied her ass off. CANNING (voice-over): Defense accident reconstructionist Charles Ruble said there was no physical evidence to back up Bonnie`s claims that Frances had hit her over and over again, no evidence he said the SUVs had even touched. RUBLE: Not even once. CANNING (voice-over): And remember how Bonnie said her purse flew forward off the seat when Frances hit her? RUBLE: This is her purse in her car. I get hit in the rear, where`s my purse go? It doesn`t come on the front. That`s simple physics. CANNING (voice-over): In fact, he said the purse falling forward supports Frances`s claims that Bonnie was repeatedly slamming on her brakes. RUBLE: She does a sudden break and she`s moving like this. Then the purse would go into the floorboard. Bonnie Contreras is not telling the truth. CANNING (voice-over): What`s more, both defense and prosecution agreed Bonnie was wrong about her contention that Bill`s motorcycle was struck from behind. Evidence showed the motorcycle actually collided with the side of Frances`s SUV. CUTTER: I can`t believe a damn thing she said on there. CANNING (voice-over): In closing arguments, the defense said Bill`s death was simply a terrible accident. And Frances Hall had suffered enough. CUTTER: She`s been living in hell for three years. Let her go home. Let her fell her family and let her warn her husband. CANNING (voice-over): But the prosecution told the jury, Frances must be held accountable for her actions. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Of course, the defendant hated Bonnie Contreras. We don`t blame her for that, any wife would. What we do blame her for getting in her Escalade chasing after Bonnie and then veering into Bill. There`s your felony murder. CANNING (voice-over): The jury deliberated into the night. Who would they believe? HOLT (voice-over): Coming up, the verdict. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: We the jury find the defendant -- HOLT (voice-over): And then this story about death on the highway takes off in a brand new direction. [22:49:57] CONTRERAS: How many more bombshells is there going to be? (COMMERCIAL BREAK) CANNING (voice-over): The jury deciding Frances Hall`s fate deliberated into the evening hours of September 8th, 2016. And then, just before 8:45, a verdict. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: We, the jury, find the defendant, Frances Hall, guilty of murder -- CANNING (voice-over): Guilty of murder and aggravated assault. Frances`s friends and family were shocked. H. HALL: It was the worst feeling in my life. It was a moment Frances herself did not seem prepared for. But things weren`t over yet for Frances, there was still a second phase of trial sentencing. Texas law allows the defendant to be sentenced by either the judge or the jury. Frances chose the jury, the same one that found her guilty. As her attorneys made the case for leniency, they found a secret weapon and the Texas criminal code. CUTTER: We said this caveat this was written for Frances Hall, if any whatever. [22:55:01] CANNING (voice-over): The law calls it sudden passion, essentially that the defendant was immediately provoked to a degree of anger that would make an ordinary person incapable of cool reflection. That offense told the jury sudden passion gripped Frances when she spotted Bill and Bonnie on the road. CUTTER: She sees this woman who has not led up and tried to ruin her life for the last month. CANNING (voice-over): The stakes were enormous. A finding of sudden passion could drastically reduce Frances`s sentence from possible life in prison to a maximum of 20 years and a minimum of just two. For the first time, the jury heard from Frances Hall directly. F. HALL: You don`t understand, I love this man hearted whole. I gave him my life. I would have never hurt him, never. CANNING (voice-over): In her final arguments, Defense Attorney Leigh Cutter insisted Frances Hall`s actions were a textbook example of sudden passion. CUTTER: The text messages, the calls, the taunting, those would probably make you really hate someone, but never having seen them until their drive by in your car. If that`s not sudden passion, where you are incapable of thinking clearly I don`t know what it is. CANNING (voice-over): But prosecutor Scott Simpson told jurors not to be swayed by emotions. SIMPSON: You shouldn`t for one second, feel ashamed or bad for doing what you believe to be right. CANNING (voice-over): After about three hours of deliberations, the jury was ready. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: We unanimously find the defendant caused the death of Bill Hall under the immediate influence of sudden passion. We assess her punishments return for two years. CANNING (voice-over): Two years, the absolute minimum sentence. On September 7th, 2018, after serving her time, Frances walked out of prison a free woman. We thought that this was the end of the story, but we were wrong. There`s a whole new chapter. This summer Frances was indicted in a multimillion dollar fraud scheme. She`s accused of providing false payroll information to get lower insurance premiums for the company she and Bill founded. The Texas Department of Insurance said the scheme allowed the company and its owners to avoid more than $9 million in premium payments. We plan to speak with Frances in person this week, but due to COVID concerns we met via Zoom. She denies the charges and the indictment. F. HALL: I`m an honest woman. I didn`t do anything illegal. I didn`t falsified anything. I`m innocent. I don`t have anything to hide. CONTRERAS: How many more bombshells is there going to be? CANNING (voice-over): We also caught up again with Bonnie Contreras to hear her thoughts on Frances`s latest troubles. CONTRERAS: She looks like a liar. She looks like a con. She just -- she looks bad all the way around. CANNING (voice-over): Bonnie now runs some businesses of her own, including a CBD spa. She believes the new charges just might change some people`s perceptions of Frances and herself. CONTRERAS: They were constantly calling me a gold digger. So who looks like the gold digger now? Is it me? Or is it her? F. HALL: I don`t even think she knows what the word gold digger means. What I`m going through right now has nothing to do with gold digging. Now what she did on her free time with my husband, that`s gold digging. I have Bill`s kids, I have Bill`s grandkids, something she`ll never have. And I have all the memories of Bill. That`s not a gold digger. That`s a wife. So she should have maybe looked it up on the dictionary first. CANNING (voice-over): Frances told us if the new case goes to trial, she`ll take the stand. It worked for her at the sentencing hearing in Bill`s murder. But insurance fraud is a serious crime too. And there`s no sudden passion defense. If convicted. The woman who served just two years for killing her husband will face the possibility of life in prison yet again. [22:59:16] HOLT (voice-over): That`s all for this edition of Dateline. We`ll see you again next Friday at 9:00, 8:00 Central as we begin our 31st season with all new two our mysteries. And of course, I`ll see you each week night for NBC Nightly News. story_text: [09:00:18] (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) CHUCK TODD, NBC NEWS HOST " (voice over): This Sunday, my interview with Vice President Kamala Harris . The vice president opens up on the threat posed by election deniers... VICE PRESIDENT KAMALA HARRIS: I think that we have to admit that there are attacks from within and we need to take it seriously. TODD: ... on the rightward shift of the Supreme Court... HARRIS: I think this is an activist court. TODD: ... and its abortion decision. HARRIS: It is not right that we take a constitutional right from the women of America and deprive them of the ability to make decisions about their own body and instead say the government`s in a better position to do that. TODD: ... on eliminating the filibuster for abortion and voting rights. HARRIS: And the president has been very clear. He will sign into law and not let the filibuster get in the way. TODD: ... on January 6th and those top-secret documents at Mar-a-Lago... (on camera): What do you say to the argument that it would be too divisive for the country to prosecute a former president? (voice over): ... and on her plans for 2024. Plus, with less than two months to go to the midterms, independent voters speak out on whether President Biden should run for re-election... (on camera): Wow, you guys are all nos. (LAUGHTER) (voice over): ... and what they think of today`s GOP. UNIDENTIFIED INDEPENDENT VOTER: I just -- I don`t recognize that party anymore. TODD (on camera): Joining me for insight and analysis are former Democratic senator Claire McCaskill; Yamiche Alcindor, moderator of "Washington Week" on PBS ; Republican political consultant Matt Gorman; and Amy Walter, editor in chief of The Cook Political Report. Welcome to Sunday. It`s "MEET THE PRESS." ANNOUNCER: From NBC News in Washington, the longest-running show in television history, this is MEET THE PRESS with Chuck Todd. TODD: And a good Sunday morning. There`s been no shortage of unkind things said about the job of vice president of the United States. And many of those things have been said by vice presidents. The most famous may have come from the first, John Adams. "I am vice president," he said. "In this I am nothing, but I may be everything." The number one job of the vice president is to be a good number two, to help make progress without making waves. And after 20 months, Kamala Harris is familiar with the position`s unique challenges. She was seen as a new symbol of a racially diverse country. But as President Biden`s approval ratings fell, so did hers. She`s been tasked with some intractable assignments, from enacting national voting reform to solving the immigration crisis at the border. Some of her supporters -- and there are quite a few -- argue she`s being set up to fail on some of those issues. But she`s also well positioned to become president someday. Why? Fifteen vice presidents already have, including our current president, who was a former vice president. Today is September 11th. It was 21 years ago that we were attacked by foreign terrorists. Not quite 20 years after 9/11 the capital came under attack from domestic terrorists. With the 9/11 anniversary in mind, I sat down with Vice President Harris on Friday at the Johnson Space Center in Houston. She was there to talk about the space program in general and to speak with some astronauts on the International Space Station. I began by asking the vice president about how, over two decades, our focus has had to shift from foreign terror to the threat from within. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) HARRIS: I think it is very dangerous. And I think it is very harmful. And it makes us weaker. You know, I`ve -- I have met with and I`ve had conversations with over 100 foreign heads of state, presidents, prime ministers, chancellors, kings. And, you know, when we as the United States walk into those rooms around the world, we have had the honor and privilege, historically, of holding our head up as a defender and an example of a great democracy. And that then gives us the legitimacy and the standing to talk about the importance of democratic principles, rule of law, human rights. And one of the things, though, that comes with that privilege is that we hold ourselves out to be a role model, which means the rest of the world, like any role model, watches what we do to see if it matches up with what we say. So you look at everything from the fact there are 11 people right now running for secretary of state, the keepers of the integrity of the voting system of their state, who are election deniers. You`ve got... TODD: And what`s that sending -- what message does that send to the world? HARRIS: Well, you couple that with people who hold some of the highest elected offices in our country who -- who refuse to condemn an insurrection on January 6th. [09:05:08] And I think what it sends is a signal that is -- that causes people to question, hey, is America still valuing what they talk about, which is the integrity of democracies, which means protecting rule of law and the -- and then sanctity of these systems and speaking up when they are attacked. And I`m -- and I`m very concerns about it, Chuck. I`ll tell you, I`m very concerned about it, because there are so many issues going on in the world that I think require at least how we as Americans have traditionally thought about what is right, what is good, what should be fought for, what should be human ideals, and certainly the ideals of democracies. And I think that, through the process of what we`ve been through, we`re starting to allow people to call into question our commitment to those principles. And that`s a shame. TODD: Nearly 70 percent of Republicans don`t believe that the president and yourself won this -- the 2020 election legitimately. Do you think you`ll ever be able to change their minds? HARRIS: I find that polling interesting. And I`m going to tell you why. I`m traveling the country. We`re here in Houston. I was in, you know, North Carolina. I was -- I mean, I`ve been traveling all over the country. I don`t find that. I don`t get that kind of sense or feedback. TODD: Do you think you talk to a lot of Republicans? (CROSSTALK) HARRIS: Well, I think I talk to a lot of Americans. And I`ll tell you, when -- when I talk to folks and they know that, for example, there was a bipartisan infrastructure law that, you know, in Durham, is going to fix I- 40, or here in Houston is going to fix Telephone Road, those are some of their priorities. When I talk to people about what we`re doing, that we`re going to make sure, especially after the pandemic, that all families, all working families, have access to affordable, high-speed internet, and they`re going to -- we`re going to bring the cost of it down, less $30 a month, plus people are going to get a $100 voucher to buy a laptop or, you know, an iPad, people want to hear that. Look what happened in Kansas, on the issue of choice. People, whoever they voted for in the last election or in the next, stood up and said, "It is not right that we take a constitutional right from the women of America and deprive them of the ability to make decisions about their own body, and instead say the government`s in a better position to do that. TODD: It`s -- you say you take issue with this idea that there are 70 percent. Do you think... HARRIS: I just don`t experience that. TODD: You don`t experience it. You don`t know if they exist? HARRIS: I think that there... TODD: Or do you think they just say it? HARRIS: Well, I`m no t-- I would not dare tell anyone what they should think. I`m just telling you that I do believe that, when it comes down to the things that wake people up in the middle of the night, that worry them about their future, about their family, about their children or their parents, most of those issues they think of not through the lens of the party with which they`re registered to vote. TODD: What is a semi-fascist? HARRIS: Listen, I think that, when we -- let`s not get caught up in -- in politicizing the fact that most people in America know that it is not helpful to our country when we have people who are denying elections or trying to obstruct the outcome of an election, where the largest number of people in our country voted for the president of the United States. And when we look at where we are, I think that we have to admit that there are attacks from within, to your first question, and we need to take it seriously. And -- and we need to stand up together, all of us, and think of this not through partisan lens but as Americans. TODD: I think back to the president`s inaugural address. And he said the following. Politics need not be a raging fire destroying everything in its path. And then I think about the construction, the language construction he used with "semi-fascist." And I understand the dilemma. You`ve got to call it out in order to bring the country together. But it`s hard to do both at the same time, isn`t it? HARRIS: Well, here`s the thing. I mean, let`s talk about our president for a moment. Joe Biden has spent his entire career -- it is on for all to see -- working across the aisle, his whole career. Sometimes he`s been criticized for believing in bipartisanship, for believing in compromise, for believing in working across the aisle, finding common ground. His whole career has been that. But there are moments in time when we have to also agree, all good people who care about our country, that there are those who right now are vividly not defending our democracy. [09:10:13] And I think we want that our commander in chief, that the president of the United States will speak up and raise the alarm about what this means to our strength and our future, much less our integrity. TODD: I`m curious, when you see the Democratic Party and some parts of the party funding ads to promote some of these election deniers in primaries, whether it`s Michigan, the high-profile race there, Illinois, Colorado, New Hampshire. It looks like a cynical -- you know, a little bit cynical. And the president went out of his way to say there are good Republicans here. Should you leave the good Republicans alone in a primary? Is the Democratic Party making a mistake here by -- by, you know, those people could win, if you`re not careful? HARRIS: I mean, listen, I`m not going to tell people how to run their campaigns. You know, I ran -- in terms of statewide office, I ran... TODD: Would you have done this? HARRIS: I ran -- I ran... TODD: Would you have done this? Is this in your -- is this something you`d be comfortable doing? HARRIS: I`m not going to tell people how to run their campaigns, Chuck. I ran for statewide, for attorney general, re-election, won both times; for Senate, won that race. And I know that it is best to -- to let a candidate, along with their -- their advisers, let them make the decision based on what they believe is in the best interest of their state. I`m not going to tell people what to do. TODD: You`re not worried that this reflects poorly on the Democrats? HARRIS: I think that what we have to focus on is that, in 60 days as of this interview, in less than two months, we are looking at a midterm election in which so much is on the line. Take, for example, the issue of choice. The United States Supreme Court , in the Dobbs decision, just took a constitutional right that had been recognized from the women of America, from the people of America. Well, how does that relate to the midterms? Our president has said he will not let the filibuster get in the way. If the Senate, through a majority vote, votes to pass the Women`s Health Protection Act, he will sign it into law. You know what that means, in the midterms? We need to hold on to the Senate and get two more. And then we can put into law the protections of Roe v. Wade. Everything is on the line when you think about the millions of women and people in America who care about them, who understand the significance of protecting a woman`s right to make decisions about her own body, instead of her government... TODD: The Democrats get 52 Senate seats... HARRIS: ... telling her what to do. TODD: Fifty-two Senate seats or more, legislative filibuster gone, or just on this issue? ALCINDOR: Well, the key issue will be whether or not them thinking President Biden is too old outweighs them thinking that the future of our democracy is on the line. And when I talk to voters, they are -- even if, even Democrats who say, you know, Biden, he`s a little slower. He`s a little bit quieter. I`m not sure if I want to back him, when they think about the state of our democracy, they`re, like, well, that`s the bigger issue here. In our NBC poll, we saw people say that the sort of threats to democracy are their number one thing, even above cost of living. So I think if you`re a Democrat, even if you`re Joe Biden looking at this and saying, okay, I understand people think maybe I should be a little bit more lively, you`re still thinking they say -- they use the words unrecognizable, distrust, and that there should be some compromise. Those are words that I think are probably worse for Republicans, especially when you think of while we might have a minority of Republicans who don`t believe that 2020 was fair, they`re the people with the loudest voices, right? They`re the people who are still winning the elections. That`s where the candidates are. And I think that that, to me, is probably signaling that Republicans have a bigger problem here. TODD: You know, Claire, I think it was Amy Jensen, I think is her name, the middle woman in our group there. I found what she said, well, it depends on what the other side is doing, right? Her vote for Biden was exactly the premise that Biden ran on, which is he knew there were people like her that would vote for him, maybe not vote for a more progressive Democrat, but would vote for him because of Trump. MCCASKILL: And that`s what I think his Philadelphia speech was about. I think it was all about trying to invite the Amys of America -- TODD: Right. MCCASKILL: -- into the tent. TODD: Not that Amy, right? MCCASKILL: Not that Amy. TODD: Right, right. Yes. MCCASKILL: The Amy that you interviewed in Arizona. I think that`s what it was about. But I will tell you, I do think the Democratic Party is struggling with an issue that is real. And that is that all of our leadership, and I say this as somebody who`s ancient, you know -- TODD: That`s us. MCCASKILL: -- a lot of old folks -- TODD: Yeah. MCCASKILL: -- are running the Democratic Party now in every part of the Democratic Party. I think the Democratic Party will benefit from really doing some navel-gazing about how can we get more young people to the forefront? Because young people are going to be really important to us in 2024. TODD: You know, ironically, Matt, if Republicans have a good election night, particularly on the House side, it`s actually going to be because it does seem like House Republicans, Kevin McCarthy`s campaign arm, really went after a diverse set of candidates. GORMAN: They did a phenomenal job recruiting -- TODD: Not like the Senate side. The House side is in a much better place - - GORMAN: House side really went after it. I mean, I think a good story, a good candidate, is worth about two points on the ballot. And look, you want to talk about fundraising, we had about 20 candidates back in 2020 raise a million dollars through July 2020. Now, we have over 90. So it`s not only good on the ballot, it helps you raise money, too. TODD: Boy, it`s amazing how poor the Senate Republican candidates are compared to the House candidates. WALTER: The class. And yet, and yet -- TODD: And yet. WALTER: -- no matter what happens on Election Day this year, it is not going to impact the views of Donald Trump , right? If the Senate stays in Democratic hands, even though every single one of those Senate -- Republican Senate candidates was endorsed by Donald Trump , I do not think that that`s going to make a reassessment -- TODD: Right. WALTER: -- of whether Donald Trump should be on the ballot in 2024. TODD: Even though in every other political election -- WALTER: Absolutely. TODD: -- we`ve ever covered, that actually has mattered. WALTER: That actually matters. TODD: But with him, it defies it. Yeah. WALTER: But it didn`t -- it didn`t matter in 2021. Didn`t matter in 2022. Yeah. TODD: And this Amy has the last word. That`s all we have for today. Thank you for watching. We`ll be back next week because if it`s Sunday, it`s "MEET THE PRESS". END Content and programming copyright 2022 NBCUniversal.
