headline: Conversation With Clea Shearer, About Her Breast Cancer Journey
story_text: [08:10:00] CRAIG MELVIN: We are back. 8:12 with "Pink Power TODAY". Our special series for breast cancer awareness month. And this morning, this morning we`re checking in with our friend Clear Shearer. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE: Yes, "The Home Edit" co-founder was diagnosed with breast cancer earlier this year and she has decided to share every step in her journey, including her recent milestone of finishing chemo. HODA KOTB: Yes, throughout it all, though guys, there`s been a group of women she`s been leaning on. They talk every day but they had never met face to face until two days ago. They`re amazing women. They all came together from all across the country for a very special conversation. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CLEA SHEARER, "THE HOME EDIT" CO-FOUNDER: Look, all of your toys are so accessible. KOTB (voiceover): Clea Shearer finds joy in being a helper. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Will you guys help me? JOANNA TEPLIN, "THE HOME EDIT" CO-FOUNDER: I can`t get up there fast enough. SHEARER: Yes. TEPLIN: Like, show us the closets. SHEARER: Yes. KOTB (voiceover): She`s created a career out of it. Taking on clutter and organizing people`s lives as one half of "The Home Edit" team. SHEARER: Hey, guys. So, by now you probably read or heard that I have breast cancer. KOTB (voiceover): But after she shared her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year, Clea found herself asking for help from those who personally knew the fight she was facing. SHEARER: As you`re going through something so brutal, like chemo, everyone in your life wants to help, but there`s nothing quite like someone who`s actually been through it or going through it at the same time. KOTB (voiceover): A friend connected her to Maria Boschetti, a three-time breast cancer survivor who lives in California with her husband. The 42- year-old, who works in public relations, was first diagnosed when she was just 25. SHEARER: She`s taken so many copious notes. So, if I just say -- if I whip out any side effects she`s like, boop, boop, boop -- KOTB (on camera): Got it. SHEARER: -- page eight. She`s like, you`ll get over that real soon. KOTB (voiceover): Amy Jethway was 42 years old when she found a lump while on vacation with her boyfriend. The biotech sales account manager diagnosed with breast cancer just weeks after Clea. Their mutual friend passed along Clea`s number to Amy who lived hundreds of miles away in New Jersey. KOTB (on camera): These are strangers? People you`ve never met. SHEARER: I`ve never met them. KOTB (on camera): Just on text. Hey, girl? SHEARER: Well -- yes, literally. And I -- there are some of, you know, these women I talk to every day. If not every day, every week, and, you know, just to check in. They`re like my dear close friends. KOT (voiceover): A community connected through tough times. Dear friends who have never met. Meeting up in person for the first time. KOTB (on camera): Well, I think it`s a good time to meet them because it`s fun to text, but it`s more fun to see people in person. [08:15:00] SHEARER: Oh. Oh, my God. AMY JETHWAY, BREAST CANCER SURVIVOR: I can`t believe we get to see you. You`re real. You`re real. Oh, my God. SHEARER: It`s so good to see you. JETHWAY: I`m going to cry. Oh, my gosh. You`re so tall. KOTB (on camera): This is so cool in this moment to be sitting here. SHEARER: I can`t believe. KOTB (on camera): First of all, you haven`t met in person yet you -- SHEARER: No. Oh, my God. KOTB (on camera): -- but you know each other intimately. What did you think, Maria, when you first started connecting with Clea? MARIA BOSCHETTI, BREAST CANCER SURVIVOR: I was shocked she was so positive, right? Because it`s a terrifying time in your life. You were wanting to talk about it. You had questions but also you were -- wanting to help others. KOTB (voiceover): Others like Amy. JETHWAY: I reached out to you during your fourth AC -- SHEARER: Yes. JETHWAY: -- when you felt really horrible. SHEARER: Yes. JETHWAY: And she was so available to me. Like, that was really overwhelming to me because I was about to start my chemo journey. KOTB (voiceover): Did that make you scared or did that make you prepared? JETHWAY: I was so grateful for how open you were and how honest you were about things because if this is what`s going to happen to me, then this is going to happen. I wound up having a very different reaction with my fourth. SHEARER: I know. I was, like, so sorry. I scared you. KOTB (on camera): Oh, you were like, I`m cool. SHEARER: She was like, fine. JETHWAY: Yes. SHEARER: Meanwhile, this whole time I was, like, guys brace yourselves. It`s going to be awful. JETHWAY: Like, it aches everywhere. KOTB (voiceover): Clea`s openness about her hair loss empowering Amy as she started to lose her own. JETHWAY: I told my boyfriend, I`m going to shave this. Like, we`re -- we can do this. We can take this head on. And kind of, whatever parts of the journey you can own, you now, that`s something I got from you. KOTB (on camera): That`s important -- that`s something you got from Clea? JETHWAY: Yes. KOTB (on camera): What is that? JETHWAY: Like, owning what you can in the journey. KOTB (on camera): Were you reluctant, Clear, because there are parts that you want to share and then there are parts you want to keep. But it sounds like you were very -- SHEARER: Oh, I don`t keep much to myself. KOTB (on camera): You don`t? SHEARER: No. Hoda, you know me. I am a barrier soul kind of girl. KOTB (on camera): Yes. SHEARER: Not only did I tell everything pretty much to these ladies but, I mean, I would also tell our Instagram followers what was going on. And it made me feel understood, you know. And it`s also nice not to feel like an anomaly. KOTB (on camera): When you`re having a crummy day, you need someone who gets it. How important has that been, Maria, to have that? BOSCHETTI: It`s so important. I -- you know, I was so young the first time I was diagnosed. And I didn`t have anybody to talk to. You don`t process those emotions when you don`t have someone to talk to or ask question and that friendship. And now, you know, I was just texting Clea last night. I feel like you are this light of sunshine that`s even bringing the last eight years back in me. SHEARER: I`m sorry about that. KOTB (on camera): By the way -- BOSCHETTI: Don`t make me cry. I`m not a pretty crier. KOTB (on camera): But that`s so beautiful. That`s a really important point. BOSCHETTI: Yes, yes. KOTB (on camera): It like -- sometimes feelings lay dormant. SHEARER: Yes. JETHWAY: Yes. BOSCHETTI: Yes. KOTB (on camera): Until someone says, let`s unearth those. KOTB (voiceover): Clea, Maria, and Amy finding strength in each other and finding peace in the small things. KOTB (on camera): Everybody has their spot where they go to when they want to just, like, cleanse and clear and you all are walking in mine. This is Central Park. What`s your place, Clea? Where do you -- SHEARER: My back porch. KOTB (on camera): Your back porch? SHEARER: I have a chair. I read there. I listen to the rain there. I greet my kids after school there. KOTB (on camera): Uh-huh. SHEARER: I just -- it makes me so peaceful. KOTB (on camera): What about for you, Amy? JETHWAY: I have my one bench right on the Hudson -- SHEARER: Oh, that`s so nice. KOTB (on camera): Yes. JETHWAY: -- and that just go out. KOTB (on camera): Doing meditation, Maria, or anything that like -- BOSCHETTI: Yes. KOTB (on camera): You`re a meditator? BOSCHETTI: Yes, meditation and beach. KOTB (on camera): Meditation and beach? BOSCHETTI: Yes. KOTB (on camera): All right. So, this is a sisterhood. SHEARER: Yes. KOTB (on camera): This is something that you believe, Clea, is not for this moment. SHEARER: Uh-huh. It`s for life. KOTB (on camera): How do you know? SHEARER: You go through life and certain people enter it for a reason. I consider you one of those people, too, Hoda. Because I don`t lose friends. I only make them. So, we`ve been through something really incredible together. And also, and a little earth shattering. KOTB (on camera): Yes. SHEARER: A lot earth shattering. So, you`re stuck with me. KOTB (on camera): We`re stuck with clea. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: Wow. KOTB: So. sweet. And by the way, if you wonder if that friendship`s rear - - real, they`re planning a vacation October together. Also, Joanna, you know, Clea`s partner, was standing in the background the whole time. Weeping. Weeping. Like these friendships, the new old friendships or old friendships are all keeping her in. She also said about her hair, she talked about it. She said it`s very kind of peach fuzzy. She`s like, I`m not sure if I`m going to cover it. I think I might just -- finally, I`m free of all that stuff. SHEINELLE JONES, NBC NEWS 3RD HOUR OF TODAY, CO-HOST: I think she looks beautiful. GUTHRIE: She has posted this week, actually, about her -- why she was wearing a wig to her kids` pickup. KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: She didn`t want to embarrass them. KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: And -- this is going to make me cry. Then her daughter said, mommy, you don`t embarrass me, I think you`re beautiful. So, she started -- yes. And you took them to your special place -- KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: -- in Central Park when you went through breast cancer? KOTB: Yes, that was my spot. It was very calming to me. It`s like -- you know, there`s no green space here but that was mine. So, I used to go there and feel very peaceful. And everyone had their little spot where they felt the warm hand. So, it was beautiful. I want to say thank you, of course, to Clea. She`s amazing and Maria and Amy. We also want to thank the Kent, that`s a beautiful space in New York. We had a great conversation there. So, we want to say thank you to them. MELVIN: That was wonderful. GUTHRIE: I`m so weepy today. MELVIN: That was wonderful. KOTB: All right. Mr. Roker, take us away. ROKER: Oh, special. OK. Guys, well, we are looking at a rainy, windy day here in the northeast and parts of New England. Sunshine through the southeast on into the Gulf where it will be nice and warm. Even up to the Great Lakes, we`re looking at a flood risk through the southwest. We`re going to continue to track that. And beautiful sunshine from Seattle to San Diego. [08:20:00] That`s what`s going on around the country. Here`s what`s happening in your neck of the woods. (LOCAL NEWS) ROKER: Don`t forget, if you`re heading out the door, head out to "TODAY" show Radio Sirius XM Channel 108. But right now -- KOTB: What time is it? ROKER: -- best time of the morning. GUTHRIE: All right. ROKER: In for Carson. KOTB: Come on, Sheinelle. JONES: We have good stuff for you this morning. KOTB: OK. We`re ready. JONES: OK. So, we`re going to start with "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever". Yesterday -- have you seen this? Marvel dropped a new trailer for the highly anticipated sequel. Of course, fans have been waiting to see how the franchise will handle the passing of its leading man, Chadwick Boseman. Well, this latest preview, giving audiences a closer look at the state of Wakanda and teasing the mysterious character stepping into the "Black Panther" suit. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: We have lost the protector. Now, is our time to strike. Show them who we are. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: I can`t wait. ROKER: All right. GUTHRIE: Who`s it going to be? JONES: We don`t know. I mean, we all have our guesses. KOTB: Yes. MELVIN: I`ll tell you what we do know. KOTB: What? MELVIN: That film`s going to make about a billion dollars. ROKER: Oh, right. KOTB: Yes. MELVIN: The first two weeks of it. JONES: Oh, it`s going to be huge. KOTB: Yes. JONES: "Black Panther: Wakanda Forever" it heads to theaters next month. Who do you think it is? GUTHRIE: What did you say, Al? ROKER: I think it`s going to be Michael B. Jordan. KOTB: Michael B. Jordan. GUTHRIE: Michael B. Jordan. OK. ROKER: Yes. GUTHRIE: All right. JONES: I thought it was going to be his sister. GUTHRIE: Yes, I wondered if anyone think it would be a woman. JONES: Right. GUTHRIE: I felt like it could be. MELVIN: This -- this is why it`s going to make a billion dollars. KOTB: yes. JONES: I know. Don`t tell me if you get there before I do. GUTHRIE: Well, they`ll have to reveal it at some point. MELVIN: That`s true. JONES: All right. Well, this is another good one. So, next up "The Crown". Calling up all Prince Harrys. A recently released casting announcement that Netflix is looking for an actor to play the adolescent royal redhead. According to the online note, they`re seeking someone with a strong physical appearance, if you guys know anybody, to play Harry from 16 to 20 years old. And that`s what`s surprising to a lot of people. Apparently, no previous professional acting experience is required because they want him to really look like him. So, if you look like the Duke of Sussex or you know someone, you should throw your hat into the ring. Thank us later. The application closes next Friday and filming is scheduled to start in November. So, you`ll have to take off from or something, I don`t know. So, the clock is ticking. Do you know anybody? GUTHRIE: They have to have a posh English accent too. JONES: I mean, I bet you there`s somebody who we don`t know. Who -- this could be their next thing. GUTHRIE: A Harry doppelganger. JONES: Yes. GUTHRIE: For sure. JONES: All right. Next up, Paul and Linda McCartney. Yesterday, "Rolling Stone" co-founder, Jann Wenner stopped by "The Howard Stern Show" and revealed how he played matchmaker with one of his magazine`s photographers and a young superstar Beatle. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) HOWARD STERN, "THE HOWARD STERN SHOW" HOST: You didn`t realize Linda was a new hired to be a "Rolling Stone" photographer. She said, I want to go meet Paul McCartney . I want to photograph -- JANN WENNER , "ROLLING STONE" CO-FOUNDER: When she said, I want to (INAUDIBLE). I said, well, we don`t really need to spend the money, you know, sending you to London and cover. Why do you want to -- why do we need more Beatles. And so, just -- well, I want to meet Paul. I say, OK. You got the assignment. Go. STERN: Wow. Nice. WENNER : And then I started getting postcards from her every couple of weeks saying, you know, how she`s getting closer and then finally I got one said, we went out last night and had the most wonderful time. Thank you forever. (END VIDEO CLIP) MELVIN: Wow. JONES: How cool was that? And the rest they say is history. KOTB: Wow. JONES: That`s Jann Wenner , by the way. ROKER: Yes. KOTB: OK. Cool. JONES: All right. Next up, Lizzo. We still can`t believe this history- making moment from last week when Lizzo was invited by the Library of Congress to play President James Madison`s 200-year-old crystal flute. Well, the presidential invites keep coming. Now, Madison`s Montpelier Estate is asking the Grammy winner to perform at the president`s home turned museum in Virginia. Writing on Instagram , thanks to classically trained singer/songwriter, Lizzo. The world had the opportunity to learn about James Madison`s crystal flute and hear his beautiful music. They go on to say, we are crossing our fingers that she would consider adding us to her schedule, once home to Madison and the now famous crystal flute. So, they loved it. GUTHRIE: It`s classical -- JONES: It was controversial but they thought, you know what -- ROKER: That`s amazing. GUTHRIE: You were there last night, right? JONES: It was phenomenal. KOTB: Did she play -- JONES: She puts on a phenomenal show. KOTB: Did she play the flute? JONES: She had it on a crystal stand. I mean, it was just -- KOTB: Beautiful. JONES: -- she had the whole place on a cloud. KOTB: Oh, awesome. Awesome. JONES: Yes, we love it. We love it when she comes here to "TODAY." All right. And finally, "The Tonight Show". headline: Republicans Rally To The Defense Of Georgia Senate Candidate Herschel Walker Facing Devastating Abuse Accusations From His Own Son And A Report He Paid For An Ex-Girlfriend`s Abortion
story_text: HODA KOTB: Meantime, the midterms just over a month away and a firestorm has erupted in a key Senate race in Georgia. Herschel Walker , the former football star now Republican nominee denying a report that he paid for his ex-girlfriend`s abortion. NBC`s Kristen Welker joins us with details on this sordid tale. Hey, Kristen, good morning. KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Hoda, good morning to you. Well, campaigns always brace for the possibility of an October surprise. Well, here it is in the critical Senate race in Georgia with a new controversy surrounding Republican Herschel Walker . Now GOP sources are telling NBC News that leading senators are preparing to stand shoulder to shoulder with him on the airwaves and on the campaign trail. But will it be enough with just five weeks until the midterms? (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) WELKER (voice-over): This morning Republicans are closing ranks around former football star Herschel Walker , their embattled Senate nominee in Georgia, a swing state that`s critical to Republicans fight to win control of the Senate. After "The Daily Beast" reported Walker in 2009, urged to then girlfriend to get an abortion after he got her pregnant, then reimbursed her for the procedure and sent her a get well card. Walker who says he wants to ban abortion after 15 weeks without exceptions, is denying the allegation. H. WALKER: It is a flat out lie. I can tell you right now, I never asked anyone to get an abortion. I never pay for an abortion. WELKER (voice-over): "The Daily Beast" says the woman asked not to be identified citing privacy concerns, adding she backed up her story by providing the get well card from Walker, an abortion clinic receipt, and a bank receipt with an image of a $700 check signed by Walker. NBC News has not independently verified the documents. CHRISTIAN WALKER, HERSCHEL WALKER`S SON: Everything has been a lie. WELKER (voice-over): Walker is also facing fierce criticism from his own son, Christian, a budding conservative influencer who says the family urged him not to run quote, because we all knew some of his past. C. WALKER: Family values people. He has four kids, four different women, wasn`t in the house raising one of them. He was out having sex with other women. Do care about family values? WELKER (voice-over): Herschel Walker later tweeting, I love my son no matter what. Walker is locked in a tight race with incumbent Democratic senator Raphael Warnock who won a special election by just two percentage points last year. Many Republicans are rushing to Walker`s defense led by former President Trump who`s endorsed him now saying Walker is being slandered and maligned by Democrats. It`s not the first controversy to rock his campaign. He`s falsely claimed he was a member of law enforcement and acknowledged fathering three children out of wedlock. Walker`s ex-wife has accused him of holding a gun to her head and threatening to kill her in incident Walker has blamed on his struggle with mental health. (END VIDEOTAPE) WELKER: Now his challenger again incumbent Democratic senator Raphael Warnock, not directly responding to the controversy. Instead, he`s stressing his long standing support for abortion rights. The big question here, will all of this make a difference? It`s just too soon to tell. But in close races like this one, even a few votes in either direction, could have an impact. Hoda? KOTB: Yes, those are some stunning allegations there. Kristen Welker for us there in Washington. Kristen, thank you. GUTHRIE: Former President Trump has taken his battle over those documents seized at his Florida Country Club, all the way to the Supreme Court filing an emergency request, Mr. Trump asking the court to declare that the 103 classified documents should be reviewed by that independent observer, the special master. Well, the government is arguing that even the special masters should not see those classified documents that were kept at Mar-a- Lago because of national security. The emergency request is being handled by Justice Clarence Thomas , who has given the Department of Justice until Tuesday afternoon to respond. headline: The New Twist In The Herschel Walker Firestorm
story_text: [19:05:15] LESTER HOLT: With a little over A month until the Midterms, a growing firestorm in Georgia of a Republican Senate candidate Herschel Walker . the woman who says Walker paid for her abortion is now making a new allegation which Walker is strongly denying. Yamiche Alcindor is there. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) YAMICHE ALCINDOR, NBC NEWS WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): After a campaign event in Georgia, tonight Herschel Walker defiant. HERSCHEL WALKER (R-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: And I`m not going to back down. The stakes are way, way too high. ALCINDOR: Following the latest twist and the controversy surrounding the Republican Senate candidate and former football star. The Daily Beast reporting the unnamed woman who the legend Walker paid for her abortion more than a decade ago says she`s also the mother of one of his children. Previously, she provided the news outlet with a receipt from an abortion clinic as well as a check and a get-well card she says are from Walker. She has not revealed her name citing privacy concerns, and NBC News has not verified her story nor the documents. Walker, an abortion rights opponent, again strongly denying the accusation. WALKER: I know this is untrue. I know nothing about any woman having an abortion. ALCINDOR: But Walker`s son, Christian, has fiercely criticized his father. CHRISTIAN WALKER, SON OF HERSCHEL WALKER : Don`t lie on the lives you`ve destroyed and act like you`re some moral family man. Y`all should care about that, conservatives. ALCINDOR: Today, we pressed Walker. What`s your reaction to people so close to you, your son, a mother of your -- someone who says that she`s the mother of your kid saying that you`re lying. What`s your reaction to people so close to you saying don`t trust you? WALKER: Just like what I just said. Democrats are desperate for this seat. This seat is important. ALCINDOR: They`re your family. WALKER: They`re very desperate for to seat. I love my family. I always love my family. I`m going to win this race. ALCINDOR: The Daily Beast says the anonymous woman, a registered Democrat, who says she`d had a years-long relationship with Walker thinks his denials are quote ridiculous. Many National Republican standing by Walker slamming it, and said it`s Democratic distraction from issues like inflation and crime. SEN. TED CRUZ (R-TX): Herschel Walker is going to win that race. This is an effort from Democrats to hold on to power. ALCINDOR: But some state Republican starting to voice their unease. LT. GOV. GEOFF DUNCAN (R-GA): Even the most staunch Republicans I think are rattled at the continued flow of information. ALCINDOR: Meanwhile, voters in Georgia sounding off. IKEDA: Still, there`s room for the consumer to benefit this holiday season. Major retailers are now trying to clear their shelves that this year are overstocked. Nike says its North America inventories up 65 percent compared to last year. That means steep discounts for bargain hunters. Everyone is looking for a deal right now. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: We`re trying to stretch our money as far as we can possibly stretch it. IKEDA: To luring cautious customers, retailers including Kohl`s and Target jumpstarted their holiday deals today. And for the first time, Amazon will hold a second prime day-like event within one year. So, when sorting through the savings, shopping experts say, compare prices online. Look for retailers who offer price matching and use a cashback credit card to stretch your dollar the furthest as inflation curbs the power of your paycheck. Emily Ikeda, NBC News New York. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: And up next, the 100-year-old Marathon Man inspiring America. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) HOLT: Finally, we want to introduce you to a 100-year-old who has truly gone the distance and shows no sign of slowing down. Maggie Vespa with "INSPIRING AMERICA." (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) MAGGIE VESPA, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): Runners often strive to outpace time. MIKE FREMONT, 100-YEAR-OLD RUNNER: The nice thing about running at this age -- VESPA: Mike Fremont defies it. FREMONT: -- is that there`s very little competition. VESPA: At 100, the retired Cincinnati engineer and great grandfather of four logs five to 10 miles three times a week. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: You are so sweet. VESPA: His 14-minute mile pace only slowed by starstruck fans. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: You`re an inspiration to a lot of people. VESPA: Does that feel weird to hear that you`re a celebrity? FREMONT: Absolutely embarrassing. VESPA: With 60 marathons under his feet, Mike boasts four world records, fastest marathons for his age at 80 and 90. Fastest half marathons at 90 and 91. Running started his therapy in his 30s after the loss of his first wife. FREMONT: So, starting to run and it worked. VESPA: Decades later, after battling cancer, Mike went vegan and with the encouragement of his second wife, Marilyn, ran marathon after marathon. What do you think is fueling it? MARILYN WALL, WIFE OF MIKE FREMONT: I think he can`t quit. VESPA: Proving her point, his other hobby, canoeing. Of course, racing goes to. For people who think at 100, a person should be slowing down. What do you say to that? FREMONT: I think they ought to be speeding up. VESPA: Proof no matter your age, your best time may still lie ahead. Maggie Vespa, NBC News, Cincinnati. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: And he just keeps going. That`s NIGHTLY NEWS for this Thursday. headline: Embattled Republican Senate Candidate Herschel Walker Defiant In The Face Of New Accusations From The Ex-Girlfriend Who Claims He Paid For Her To Have An Abortion
story_text: KRISTEN WELKER: All right, well, now to several new twists and what is arguably the most closely watched Senate race of next month`s midterm elections. Overnight, Georgia`s Republican Senate candidate Herschel Walker , speaking out to NBC News and standing by his claims that he didn`t know an ex-girlfriend had an abortion more than a decade ago. This is the same woman now says Walker wanted her to have a second abortion years later but she refused. NBC`s Allie Raffa is following all of these developments from Atlanta for us this morning, Allie, good morning to you. [07:10:00] ALLIE RAFFA, NBC NEWS CAPITOL HILL CORRESPONDENT: Kristen, good morning. Democrats controlled the Senate by just the thinnest of margins and keeping that hold could easily come down to this crucial Peach State Senate race where in just a few days has gone from too close to call to downright roiled in allegations. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) RAFFA (voiceover): This morning, all eyes on Georgia, the crucial Senate race between Trump-back to Republican Herschel Walker and incumbent Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock roiled in controversy after bombshell allegations this week by The Daily Beast that Walker paid for a former girlfriend`s abortion in 2009. And a New York Times report Friday that Walker pressured this same woman to have another abortion two years later, but she refused. Walker, who`s running on a staunch anti-abortion platform, repeatedly denying both claims. HERSCHEL WALKER , REPUBLICAN SENATE CANDIDATE, GEORGIA: I`m not going to back down. These things are way, way too high. RAFFA: But in a new twist overnight, the former football star confirming to NBC directly that his wife and the woman making the allegations revealed to be the mother of one of his children, were in contact Friday morning, the woman telling Walker`s wife that he paid for her abortion. Walker sharing copies of the text exchange with NBC News and saying "I`m not saying she did or didn`t have one. I`m saying I don`t know anything about that. I don`t know." Walker telling NBC this was the first time the woman ever mentioned the abortion to him or his wife. But the woman showed the New York Times and The Daily Beast a copy of a receipt from an Atlanta abortion clinic. A check that she claimed was reimbursement for the procedure. And the get well card she claims came from the former football star. We should note we have not seen this documentation. Walker telling NBC News "I don`t remember any card or check or anything. But I was dating her. I could have sent some money. I could have sent a card. But not for the reasons she is saying." Despite the spectacle, most congressional Republicans are still backing Walker. SEN. TED CRUZ, (R-TX): Herschel Walker is going to win that race. This is an effort from Democrats to hold on to power. RAFFA: While state Republicans` frustrations only grow. LT. GOV. GEOFF DUNCAN, (R-GA): Even the most staunch Republicans I think are rattled at the continued flow of information. RAFFA: Just 32 days before voters have their say. (END VIDEOTAPE) RAFFA: As of now, Walker doesn`t have any plans this weekend to meet with voters. But ultimately the choice is theirs. Republicans here tell me they don`t think this controversy will have any impact on this Senate race, while Democrats say this is just another reason they don`t think Walker is fit for Office, Kristen, Peter. WELKER: Allie Raffa, at the center of the political universe right now in Atlanta, thank you. END Content and programming copyright 2022 NBCUniversal. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. [09:00:19] (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) KRISTEN WELKER, GUEST HOST OF NBC`S "MEET THE PRESS WITH CHUCK TODD" (voice over): Our issues this Sunday, October surprises. In Ukraine President Vladimir Putin faces a huge setback after an explosion damages a bridge to a critical supply line to Crimea, as President Biden warning the risk of a nuclear attack is at its highest level since the Cuban missile crisis. UNKNOWN: We are closer to a potential use of a nuclear weapon. WELKER: In the Senate race in Georgia, Republican hopeful Herschel Walker denies allegations he paid for an ex-girlfriend`s abortion. HERSCHEL WALKER , (R) GEORGIA SENATE CANDIDATE: The abortion thing is false. It`s a lie. (PROTESTERS CHANTING) WELKER: Abortion rights now taking center stage in a race that could determine which party controls the Senate. SEN. RAPHAEL WARNOCK , (D) GEORGIA: The people of Georgia need a senator who will stand with women. WELKER: And gas prices could spike ahead of Election Day after OPEC cuts oil production, putting Democrats on the defensive. PRESIDENT JOSEPH R. BIDEN, JR.: I was able to bring down gasoline down well over $1.60, but it`s inching up because of what the Russians and the Saudis just did. WELKER: I`ll speak with Republican Congressman Don Bacon of Nebraska and Democratic congresswoman Elissa Slotkin of Michigan. Plus, presidential portrait. FORMER PRESIDENT DONALD J. TRUMP: It helps when you`ve done nothing wrong. WELKER: Maggie Haberman of the New York Times and author of the new book "Confidence Man" is here with her new reporting on the former president`s document fight and an in-depth look at his rise to power, including Donald Trump`s changing views on abortion, reversing the position he once made right here on this program. TRUMP : I`m very pro-choice. WELKER (on camera): Joining me for insight and analysis are Yamiche Alcindor, moderator of "Washington Week" on PBS ; former White House press secretary Jen Psaki ; and Republican strategist Brendan Buck. Welcome to Sunday. It`s "Meet the Press." ANNOUNCER: From NBC News in Washington, the longest-running show in television history, this is "Meet the Press With Chuck Todd." WELKER: Good Sunday morning. I`m Kristen Welker, in for Chuck Todd. Election Day is just 30 days away. And that means 30 more days of October and November surprises. The term "October surprise" was coined during the 1980 presidential campaign. Ronald Reagan worried Jimmy Carter would engineer a last-minute release of U.S. hostages held in Iran. Carter, of course, did not, but the term stuck. There are at least three stories unfolding that may produce a surprise this cycle, first the nuclear threat from Russia. President Biden warned in a private fund-raiser this week that "We have not faced the prospect of Armageddon since the Cuban Missile Crisis" in 1962. Then there are rising gas prices, now averaging just under $4 a gallon, which Democrats worry will be a sign to voters that there is trouble in the economy. But it is of course the Georgia Senate race which produced the October surprise of the week, since it could determine the control of Senate. Herschel Walker , the Republican nominee who`s been running as an anti- abortion candidate, opposing abortion even in cases of rape or incest, spent the week denying allegations by a woman that he paid for her abortion in 2009. She now tells the New York Times he urged her to terminate a second pregnancy two years later. They ended their relationship when she refused. The woman, who is also the mother of one of his four children, shared a $575 receipt for her abortion procedure and a copy of a check from Walker reimbursing her, as well as a "get well" card he allegedly signed. Over the week, Walker`s explanations have evolved. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) WALKER: I never asked anyone to get an abortion. I never paid for an abortion. And it`s a lie. UNKNOWN: Here`s the card. And you signed it. Is that you? WALKER: That -- that`s why I`ve said (inaudible) that looks like my signature. First of all, I never just put an "H" on anything. I never have. If that had happened, I would have -- I would have said it. You know, there`s nothing to be ashamed of there. You know, people have done that. But I know nothing about it. QUESTION: You said that, if this did happen, there`s nothing to be ashamed of. How do you square that... WALKER: I never said -- I never said... QUESTION: You said it this morning on (inaudible) show. WALKER: No, what I said -- I was talking about something totally different than did it happen. I said, when I -- with my ex-wife, in my past, nothing to do with what this woman said. QUESTION: So you`re saying that... WALKER: I said this -- this here, the abortion thing is false; it`s a lie. If anything happened, that`s nothing to be ashamed of because my ex-wife and I have been the best of friends with her husband and my wife. (END VIDEOTAPE) WELKER: Republicans have largely stood by Walker, as Texas Senator Ted Cruz told my colleague Vaughn Hillyard, "I want every Republican running for Senate in this country to win." I`m joined now by Republican Congressman Don Bacon of Nebraska, whose toss- up race for re-election is one of NBC`s most consequential races to watch. Congressman Bacon, welcome back to "Meet the Press." REP. DON BACON (R-NE): Well, thank you, Kristen. Thanks for having me back on. WELKER: It is good to see you. I do want to start right there in Georgia, the headlines this week. [09:05:05] Given everything that we have seen, do you support Herschel Walker ? BACON: Well, I sure do, more for the policy positions he`s going to take. Senator Warnock is one of the most liberal, progressive folks. He wants abortion on demand until birth. Only one in five voters support that. Now, Herschel needs to be -- come clean and just be honest. We also know that we all make mistakes. And it`s just better if it -- if this actually did happen, say "I`m sorry" and ask for forgiveness. But this is also... WELKER: But... (CROSSTALK) BACON: ... about positions. WELKER: But, Congressman, let me ask you. BACON: And... WELKER: Let me ask you this, though, Congressman. by supporting Herschel Walker , given these allegations, is the GOP, are you sending a message that Republicans are willing to win at all costs? BACON: Well, I think people mistakes. And if people acknowledge them and ask forgiveness, none of us are perfect. And also, we`ve got to realize that Senator Warnock has his own allegations. WELKER: But he hasn`t acknowledged that this is one of his mistakes. Do you want to hear more from him on this issue? It sounds like you still have questions. BACON: Well, I think it`s just best to be candid. I`ve learned that in my own life, be candid; be honest. But in the end this is going to be about policy positions. Senator Warnock is one of the most liberal people in the Senate. He wants abortion on demand until birth. Only one in five voters support that. WELKER: But do the allegations... BACON: There`s also allegations against Senator -- well, let me get a word in here, or two, on this. Senator Warnock has his own allegations. What about spousal abuse? There are allegations out there, too. So I hope the media does just as much attention on these allegations on Senator Warnock and what his wife, his ex-wife, said he was -- she was abused by him. So I hope you`re showing some equal opportunity here with both these candidates. WELKER: And those are allegations that he, of course, has denied as well. But let me ask you more broadly speaking. Does this undercut the Republican Party`s broader message of being anti-abortion, when you have these conflicting things happening with Herschel Walker ? BACON: I think you`ve just got to stand on principle here. When I -- when I look at our own race right now... WELKER: But does it undercut that principle, Congressman? Does it undercut that principle? BACON: It -- it can undercut. You want to walk the talk and talk the walk. You want to have cohesion with your message. But people also make mistakes. I`m surely not -- I`m not a flawless person by no means. I have made my own mistakes in life. And Herschel has, too. We all have. I think it`s better just to be honest. But in the end, Americans do not want abortion on demand until birth. And I think that that`s the principle tjhat we need to focus on as a Republican Party. The average voter -- and I have seven different polls -- would like to see restrictions at about the 15-week point. I -- that`s where Europe is at right now; Germany`s at there -- is there. Our policies at the federal level are aligned with China and North Korea. And that`s where Senator Warnock`s at. That`s where my opponent`s at. WELKER: Let me follow up with you on that point then. Can you say point- blank that you support Senator Lindsey Graham`s proposal for a federal ban on abortion after 15 weeks? BACON: On principle I do. Because I think most voters support a 15-week ban. It`s where Europe is at. Most free countries have gone there. But the reality is the Senate will not be able to pass that because of the 60-vote -- you know, the filibuster. So most of these decisions are going to be made at the state level. Because that`s where decisions can be made. Whether you have a pro-abortion majority in the House and Senate or a pro- life majority in the Senate or House, you`re not going to get back the 60- vote threshold in the Senate. WELKER: Well... BACON: So the reality is most of it`s going to be done at the state level. WELKER: But, Congressman, and I hear you, but I think a lot of people would be interested in the fact that you support this 15-week ban at the federal level, because Republicans have been arguing for 50 years now that this should be a states` issue. Now you`re going against that? BACON: Well, the voters get to decide and they get to decide by selecting representatives at the state and the federal level. But on principle, I believe in the humanity of the unborn child. I think the science has taken us way beyond where Roe v. Wade had us. That`s why -- Roe v. Wade prohibited states from going the 15-week restrictions, for example. And most of the free world has -- has left America behind. The free world has seen the science of the unborn child and they`ve moved more towards a more reasonable policy of 12 to 15 weeks. I do believe America should go the same direction. WELKER: Well, let me follow up with you on that, because you co-sponsored the Life at Conception Act, which would effectively have given a fetus constitutional rights from the moment of fertilization. So why now support legislation that would allow over 90 percent of abortions to occur? BACON: Well, on principle I am pro-life. And I`m always going to defend the humanity of the unborn. Now, the... WELKER: But isn`t supporting a 15-week ban in contradiction to also supporting the idea that a fetus has constitutional rights at conception? BACON: Well, I want to -- I want to move us forward. You know, we have too many people in Washington that say "I want -- I demand 100 percent," and they won`t take 50 percent or 40 percent. I believe I want to move us in the right -- we want to move the right direction here. And I do believe in the personhood of the unborn. [09:10:01] However, this same law doesn`t prohibit state legislatures or the federal government to put in various restrictions or exceptions. It just says on principle the unborn child has humanity. And I believe that. But it still gives legislators the right to restrict or provide exceptions. But the American voters right now are at 12 to 15 weeks. I accept that reality and I want to move us forward. WELKER: Congressman, let`s talk about foreign policy. This week -- of course you serve on the House Armed Services Committee . You are a decorated Air Force veteran. We all learned this week that President Biden, at a closed-door fund-raiser with Democrats, warned of a nuclear Armageddon. Is that consistent with your perspective? Is that your assessment of the threat right now? BACON: I do think Vladimir Putin is a cornered animal. I think he is, right now, unpredictable, unstable. He is getting beat in Ukraine, piece by piece. And he`s -- he`s being embarrassed. His country`s being embarrassed, not only by being defeated but the barbaric behavior of his country in Ukraine, stealing their grain, sexually assaulting their women, murdering just innocent people. This is the view the world has towards Russia and Putin. But I think he`s a cornered animal right now. He`s unstable. But you can`t let this guy threaten us and bully us around. Because if you cave out of fear, he`ll do it again. WELKER: Let me turn to... BACON: So we just -- we`ve got to stand firm with him... WELKER: Go ahead. Go ahead, finish, Congressman. BACON: Well, we`ve just got to stand firm. We`ve got to stand firm towards him. You can`t let a bully push you around. I also do think President Biden`s got to be more careful, though. Throwing down the "nuclear Armageddon" was a little too flippant. President of France Macron chided him on it. And I think the president needs to be more cautious. WELKER: Let me ask you about another campaign issue. Obviously the issue of crime has loomed large. I want to ask you about some comments that we heard from Senator Tommy Tuberville overnight at a rally with former President Trump. Take a listen. I`ll get your reaction on the other side. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) SEN. TOMMY TUBERVILLE (R-AL): Some people say, well, they`re "soft on crime." No, they`re not soft on crime; they`re pro-crime. They want crime. They want crime, because they want to take over what you`ve got. They want to control what you have. They want reparation, because they think the people that do the crime are owed that. (Bleep). (END VIDEO CLIP) WELKER: Are those comments appropriate for a sitting U.S. senator, Congressman? BACON: Well, I wouldn`t say it the same way. But there is a problem in our country with crime. Major cities have seen a 40 to 50 percent increase in violent crime. And the primary reason, in my view, is we have these far- left prosecutors, county attorneys and mayors who are releasing violent criminals back on the street. WELKER: But, Congressman... (CROSSTALK) WELKER: Congressman, there is a different way to say that. I mean, most people heard those comments... BACON: I would be more polite. WELKER: ... and felt -- not just polite, but a lot of people heard those comments as being racist. BACON: Yeah, I`m -- that`s not the way I present things, but we`ve got to be honest that we have a crime problem in our country... WELKER: But -- but do you feel as though those comments... BACON: ... prosecutors releasing... WELKER: ... crossed a racial line, Congressman? Do they cross a racial line? BACON: Oh, I don`t -- I don`t -- I`m not going to say he`s being racist. But I wouldn`t use that language, be more polite. But the fact is we can`t ignore we have a 40 percent to 50 percent violent crime increase. And it`s because Democrat politicians and prosecutors are putting violent criminals back on the street early. And it`s unacceptable. When a guy commits a crime the first time, shame on them. When society releases that same criminal and they create more victims, that`s shame on us for allowing that to happen. WELKER: Let me ask... BACON: And too many Democrat politicians are releasing these criminals on the street. WELKER: Let me ask you very quickly about what is happening inside your own party. According to our NBC News political unit, 219 House Republican candidates have actively questioned or outright denied the 2020 election results. Would you be comfortable serving alongside them? BACON: Well, as you know, I certified the election. I supported the bipartisan commission. I condemned the violence that day. And so I just stand on my own record. You know, districts get to elect their own people. We have had people on the other side of the aisle call the 2016 election illegitimate. Hillary Clinton did that. We have the -- the lady for Georgia who lost her election still has not conceded defeat from two years ago, or four years ago. So both sides are -- are guilty. I don`t like the hypocrisy, though, of focusing on just one side on the elections. I believe in protecting our elections. I have voted that way. I`ve spoke that way. But we tend to, and our media tends to focus on just the Republican part here, when you have Hillary Clinton also questioning the legitimacy of the 2016 election. WELKER: Congressman -- all right, well, let me ask you... BACON: Yes. WELKER: ... last time you were on this show, you told Chuck that you would not support former President Trump for the Republican nomination in 2024. But I want to ask you, if he is the party`s nominee, will you vote for him? BACON: We`ll get - when we get to that point, I`ll -- I`ll let you know. In the meantime, we`re going to have this election... WELKER: You`re up for re-election... BACON: ... in 30 days. WELKER: ... right now, Congressman. A lot of voters want to know where you stands on this issue. Will you supports former President Trump if he`s the nominee in 2024? [09:15:17] BACON: I have made my point for the primary. That`s as far as I want to go right now. In the end, we`ve got to win in November and take back the House and the Senate, to stop Joe Biden`s policy. We need to force him back in the middle. That is where my focus is at. WELKER: All right. Congressman Bacon, thank you so much... BACON: Thank you. WELKER: ... for joining "Meet the Press." Really appreciate it. And Democratic Congresswoman... BACON: Yes, ma`am. WELKER: ... Elissa Slotkin of Michigan joins me now. Her race is also rated a toss-up. Welcome back to "Meet the Press." REP. ELISSA SLOTKIN (D-MI): Thanks for having me. WELKER: So I want to ask you about the political drama that is unfolding in Georgia. I was just talking about it with Congressman Bacon. And I want to ask you about the response from the Democratic incumbent, Raphael Warnock , who has decided not to directly attack Herschel Walker , to address, really, these claims repeatedly on the campaign trail. Given the high stakes of Georgia, is that a mistake, Congresswoman? SLOTKIN: I don`t know. I mean, I think what Mr. Walker is doing himself is enough for voters to see, right? He`s being accused of something. He`s not admitting it, or he`s dodging. People are saying that he -- you know, people make mistakes, but he`s not admitting that mistake. I think just -- I understand the instinct to just let him stand in the spotlight and answer for his own record and not take that as a moment to just, kind of, double down on the attack. WELKER: OK, well, abortion is obviously an issue that you care a lot about. You have talked quite a bit about it. And abortion is actually on the ballot in your state. In fact, the ballot proposal would enshrine a right to an abortion. And opponents argue the problem with it is that it`s too wide-ranging, that there are no limits on third trimester abortions. So let me put this question to you directly, Congresswoman. Would you like to see limits on third trimester abortions? SLOTKIN: Yeah. I mean, the ballot initiative that we have says that you can have the right to an abortion up to the point of viability, and then afterwards it has to be because of the health of the mother deemed by a medical professional. So it`s not abortion on demand. It`s not through the ninth month, all these talking points that the Republicans are using because they know they`re on their heels on this issue. So I support that ballot initiative. I think it`s written correctly, and it codifies Roe in a state where, without that, we`re facing a 1931 ban. WELKER: But, again, just on that issue of third trimester abortions, should there be restrictions to that? SLOTKIN: Yes. I -- I agree with the proposal, which says, up to viability, you have the right to make that decision on your own, but afterwards you need the input of a medical professional. I think that`s the right place for our state and, frankly, I think, for the country. WELKER: You have prided yourself on being a moderate Democrat. And I wonder if you think there is room within the conversation around abortion for Democrats who are anti-abortion, by John Bel Edwards or Representative Henry Cuellar ? SLOTKIN: Yes. I mean, I think, for me, I represent a district that`s Republican-leaning. The vast majority of my constituents identify as pro- life. And I`ve been at plenty of events, as recently as yesterday, where people will say, "Look, I am a pro-life Democrat." But I think the distinction is that they`re not trying to impose their will on this issue on other people, on other women, right? They have a personal conviction that they feel very firmly about, and I respect that, but they`re not trying to say that their will has to be imposed on the rest of all women. And I think that`s -- they have a place in this party. But I think they also will say very openly they don`t believe the government should make that decision for women. WELKER: Let`s talk about one of the top issues for voters in races all across this country right now, Congresswoman. Of course that is the economy. Republicans, including your opponent, have accused you and Democrats of overspending, whether we`re talking about the COVID relief bill or the latest Inflation Reduction Act. What do you say to that criticism, that Democrats have actually made inflation worse by overspending? SLOTKIN: Well, first of all, I think we can`t dance away from the fact that inflation is a real issue that`s affecting every single person in this country. I don`t know one family that isn`t making different decisions because of how bad inflation. And we don`t win any points by trying to pretend it`s not there. It`s there. I think, for me, there`s almost, like, a gleefulness about some Republicans, including my opponent, about how bad inflation is. There`s a gleefulness when prices of gas are going up. And I think that`s, just as a leader... WELKER: But, Congresswoman, I guess I`m asking, do Democrats bear some of... SLOTKIN: ... not the right approach. WELKER: ... of the responsibility? But do Democrats bear some of the responsibility? You control the White House, both chambers of Congress. Why shouldn`t voters hold Democrats responsibility for the economy? SLOTKIN: I -- I think they do. I think, while I think inflation is obviously a worldwide phenomenon, I am open to the fact that we have to make decisions here in the United States. Democrats are in power. We`re in the White House, in the House and the Senate, even if it`s slim margins. So, sure, I do think that there is a rightful skepticism about particularly the last COVID package. And I think that`s why you`ve seen a lot of us in Congress really shy away from another COVID package, even when the White House was proposing one this past summer. [09:20:05] So I -- I own it, but I think it has to be reflected, you know, across the world, that it`s going -- it`s a post-COVID phenomenon that we`re trying to deal with the best we can. WELKER: Let`s talk about student loan debt. Are you comfortable with President Biden`s plan to forgive student loan debt, even though it`s likely going to add $400 billion to the debt? SLOTKIN: I did not support the proposal that the president put forward or the action that the president took forward. It`s not that I don`t understand that we have a crisis of college affordability. headline: Top Republicans Traveling To Georgia To Campaign With Herschel Walker Amid His Abortion Controversy
story_text: LESTER HOLT: Just four weeks until the Midterms, today`s Senate Republican heavyweights rally behind Herschel Walker as he tries to weather the abortion controversy now overshadowing his campaign in all-important Georgia. Here`s Peter Alexander. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) PETER ALEXANDER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): Tonight, in Georgia, Republican reinforcements arriving to pollster embattled Senate nominee Herschel Walker . SEN. TOM COTTON (R-AR): It`s especially good to be here with the next United States Senator from Georgia Herschel Walker . ALEXANDER: Key senators Tom Cotton and Rick Scott standing by the former football great as he faces an allegation that he paid for an abortion for an ex-girlfriend more than a decade ago, while now campaigning on his opposition to abortion rights. Walker has strongly denied the accusation, but today for the first time publicly acknowledged he now knows who the woman is. The senators tonight insists the controversy will not cost Walker the race. SEN. RICK SCOTT (R-FL): Inflation, crime, parents not being involved in schools. That`s what people are going to vote on. ALEXANDER: Still, some state Republicans have criticized Walker. Lieutenant Governor Geoff Duncan writing, Walker has not yet earned my vote. He has four weeks left to change our minds. While, overnight, another critical clash over Ohio`s open Senate seat. In their first debate, Democratic Congressman Tim Ryan , accusing Republican J.D. Vance of lavishing praise on former President Trump. REP. TIM RYAN (D-OH): Ohio needs an ass-kicker, not an ass-kisser. ALEXANDER: While Vance attacked Ryan for voting 100 percent of the time with President Biden who remains unpopular with Ohio voters. J.D. VANCE (R-OH), SENATE CANDIDATE: We`re getting close to Halloween and Tim Ryan is put on a costume where he pretends to be a reasonable moderate. (END VIDEOTAPE) [19:10:07] ALEXANDER (on camera): Tim Ryan also tried to distance himself from President Biden saying he does not believe the President should run for reelection in 2024. Lester? HOLT: Peter, thank you. END Content and programming copyright 2022 NBCUniversal. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. Transcription Copyright 2022 VIQ Media Transcription, Inc. headline: Dr. Mehmet Oz On Crime And His Campaign`s Attacks On Fetterman`s Health
story_text: LESTER HOLT: Just 25 days before the Midterms, tonight, we speak exclusively with Dr. Mehmet Oz, the Republican facing off against Democrat John Fetterman in that critical Pennsylvania Senate race. Our Dasha Burns pressing Dr. Oz on crime and his campaign`s attacks on Fetterman`s health. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) DASHA BURNS, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): Pennsylvania Republican Senate candidate and celebrity doctor, Mehmet Oz, has focused much of his campaign on crime and blasting Democrat John Fetterman on his votes as the head of the state`s Board of Pardons. He says he believes in second chances, the former president with his First Step Act, also was about giving second chances to prisoners who deserve it. Why don`t prisoners who prove good behavior, who are modeled prisoners, why don`t they deserve second chances? MEHMET OZ (R-PA), SENATE CANDIDATE: The First Step Act had nothing to do with convicted murderers being released from prison, especially if they`ve been sentenced to life in prison. It`s a whole different game. When John Fetterman is asked, if you could wave a magic wand, what`s the one thing you would do, the one thing? And he says why get rid of life in prison? BURNS: Well, I asked him that. He actually said, it would be codifying Roe versus Wade and abolishing the Filibuster. OZ: Well, he`s answered it the way I just described in the past as well. And too often, John Fetterman seems to pay more attention to the feelings of the criminals than the innocent who were hurt. BURNS: We also asked about his campaign`s attacks on Fetterman`s health. He was off the campaign trail for months after suffering a stroke. One of your campaign staffers said that John Fetterman wouldn`t have had a stroke if he had "ever eaten a vegetable in his life." You`re a doctor. You`re a heart doctor. You of all people understand what John Fetterman is going through better than most. Why would you allow your campaign to mock him like that? OZ: I have tremendous compassion for what John Fetterman has gone through. I mean, not only do I, as a doctor, appreciate the challenges, but I know his specific ailment because it`s a specialty area of mine. BURNS: But would you ever talk to your patients like this? OZ: No. BURNS: He criticizes Fetterman for not releasing his medical records, while Fetterman accuses Dr. Oz of not being transparent on abortion rights. This is what he told us this week. JOHN FETTERMAN (D-PA), SENATE CANDIDATE: Dr. Oz likes to make fun of me that I might miss a word. But you know, he`s missed, you know, two words. And that is a yes or no on the national abortion ban. BURNS: So, we asked him about Republican Senator Lindsey Graham`s bill that would ban abortions after 15 weeks. If you win, you`re going to be a colleague of his. You`re going to have to vote on bills like this. So, can you tell us right now, yes or no on that bill? OZ: I`m giving you a bigger answer than yes or no. I`m telling you. I don`t want any federal rules limiting what states do with abortion. It should be up to the states. (END VIDEOTAPE) BURNS: Lester, there was more we wanted to discuss. We had to ask for the same amount of time Fetterman gave us about 30 minutes, but the campaign said they had time constraints, so we only spoke for about half that time. Lester? HOLT: Dasha Burns, thank you. END Content and programing copyright 2022 NBCUniversal. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. Transcription Copyright 2022 VIQ Media Transcription, Inc. headline: NBC NIGHTLY NEWS for October 14, 2022, NBC
story_text: [19:00:00] (COMMERCIAL BREAK) LESTER HOLT, NBC NEWS ANCHOR (on camera): Tonight, the search for answers after a deadly shooting rampage in North Carolina. (voiceover): A 15-year-old suspect in custody after the mass shooting that left five people dead in Raleigh. What we`re learning about the victims. Among them an off-duty police officer and a 16-year-old boy. What was the shooter`s motive? Also, tonight, the new move in the battle of her documents seized at Mar-a- Lago. What the DOJ is asking an appeals court to do regarding the special master. And Donald Trump sending a 14-page letter to the January 6 Committee after it voted to subpoena him. What it says? And the video from the day of the attack, Nancy Pelosi saying she wanted to punch Mr. Trump out. Our NBC News exclusive with Dr. Mehmet Oz, GOP Senate candidate in Pennsylvania. Does he stand by his campaign`s attacks on the health of his Democratic rival John Fetterman ? Does he support a federal ban on abortion and his anti-crime message? The holiday shopping season, why it`s off to an early start. Where to get big bargains right now? It`s America`s fastest-growing sport with fans like Tom Brady and LeBron James. How Pickleball is going pro. And remembering the actor who brought up a beloved Harry Potter character to life. ANNOUNCER: This is NBC NIGHTLY NEWS with Lester Holt. HOLT (on camera): Good evening. We are going to begin with the tragic and frightening story that was breaking in North Carolina as we came on the air here last night. We now know five people died allegedly at the hands of a teenage shooter who held a Raleigh neighborhood in fear, forcing residents to barricade themselves inside their homes. North Carolina`s Governor calling it the nightmare of every community. Authority say the alleged shooter left a two-mile trail of victims and crime scenes behind him. Tonight, the 15-year-old suspect is being held and is in critical condition after a long standoff with police. The dead include an off-duty police officer and range in age from 16 to 52. Two other people were injured. And eyewitnesses are now describing to us their own harrowing encounters with the accused shooter. Blayne Alexander is in Raleigh and has late details. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) BLAYNE ALEXANDER, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): The crime scene stretched more than two miles from his quiet Raleigh neighborhood to a nearby walking path, a literal trail of terror all left by one gunman who police say is just 15 years old. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Officer down. We have an officer down. ALEXANDER: The first chance came just after 5:00 p.m. as neighborhood kids were getting off the school bus. Nayesha Royle (PH) was at home and heard screams outside. NAYESHA ROYLE, RALEIGH RESIDENT: A neighbor`s kids were knocking banging on the door. I`m telling her like open the door. Something`s going on. And you hear the kids say he has a gun. He has a gun. There`s a gun. ALEXANDER: And when you open the door, what did you see? ROYLE: Chaos. Chaos. ALEXANDER: She also saw the gunman and frantically started pulling neighbors and schoolchildren into her house. ROYLE: If you could have seen a fear in their eyes -- like, the little girl was like, he pointed the gun at me. And they`re kids. They`re kids. ALEXANDER: For more than four hours, police combed the area, bringing dogs and helicopters and telling residents to stay inside. Finally, they say they found the gunman hiding nearby. He was taken into custody and to the hospital in critical condition. MARY-ANN BALDWIN, MAYOR, RALEIGH: There are several families in our community waking up this morning without their loved ones. ALEXANDER: Among those killed according to officials, 29-year-old Gabriel Torres, an off duty police officer headed to work, 16-year-old James Roger Thompson a high school junior, the Sue Karnatz who was out for a run. Her husband says that was her biggest passion outside of their three boys. Nicole Connors, a caregiver at heart dedicated to her husband and their dog Sammy. And 35-year-old Mary Marshall set to get married in just two weeks. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: Blayne, none of it makes sense. Did police said anything about a possible motive? ALEXANDER (on camera): Unfortunately, not yet, Lester. In fact, police are not saying what led up to that shooting, only that the entire thing is still under investigation. But we are learning more about charges. Tonight, the DA`s office confirms that even though the suspect is only 15 years old, he will be charged as an adult. Lester? HOLT: Blayne Alexander in Raleigh tonight, thank you. This evening, former President Trump`s response after the January 6 Committee voted to subpoena him as new video from inside the Capitol on that day shows the fear and frustration of congressional leaders. Kelly O`Donnell has late details. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) KELLY O`DONNELL, NBC NEWS SENIOR WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): Former President Trump used 14 pages to vent his anger, disappointment, and complaint at the January 6 Committee for not investigating his claims of election fraud rejected by courts. With crowd photos, he embraced rioters as hard-working American patriots, but no answer on whether he will comply with a subpoena to testify. [19:05:22] SEN. CHUCK SCHUMER (D-NY): You know, the Capitol has been totally overrun. Answer my question. O`DONNELL: NBC News obtained 42 minutes of documentary footage shot by Speaker Pelosi`s daughter. CNN obtained additional clips that show congressional leaders of both parties. SEN. MITCH MCCONNELL (R-KY): Get them there in one hell of a hurry. Do you understand? O`DONNELL: Scrambling to get guard troops sent to the Capitol. SCHUMER: We need them there now, whoever you got. O`DONNELL: In another exchange -- REP. NANCY PELOSI (D-CA): Hi, Mr. Vice President. O`DONNELL: Speaker Pelosi reaches Mike Pence . PELOSI: I worry about you being in that Capitol building. Don`t let anybody know where you are. O`DONNELL: From concern, to fury at President Trump. PELOSI: I want to punch him out and I`m going to go to jail, and I`m going to be happy. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: And Kelly O`Donnell joining us now. And there are also new legal developments, Kelly, in the search of the former president`s Mar-a-Lago estate. O`DONNELL (on camera): That`s right. The Department of Justice is asking an appeals court in the Mar-a-Lago documents case to end the use of an independent reviewer of those materials seized that Mr. Trump had requested. Lester? HOLT: Kelly, thank you. ALEXANDER LUKASHENKO , PRESIDENT, BELARUS (through translator): If you put a person or a country in a corner, there is only one way out from there, to move forward? As far as the subtext of your question is concerned, never. Putin and the leadership of Russia never set the goal of using a nuclear weapon in Ukraine. SIMMONS : How would you describe President Putin state of mind right now? LUKASHENKO (through translator): Is that what you think in the western United States? And this week, Lukashenko supported Russia, at the U.N . Civilians being targeted, women and children. How can Belarus justify voting against the U.N . resolution to condemn the Russian offensive? In 60 seconds, holiday sales already kicking off as spending cools down. How stores are getting you by now. So, is Black Friday a thing of the past? Here`s Miguel Almaguer with tonight`s "PRICE YOU PAY." (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: This is Black Friday now. To jumpstart consumer spending that`s falling flat as inflation hits a 40-year, high big box stores like Best Buy , Target, and Walmart are tonight trying to unload excess inventory kicking off holiday sales earlier this year. [19:15:14] KIMBERLY PALMER, PERSONAL FINANCE EXPERT, NERDWALLET : Black Friday has already started because the sales have begun, the discounts have already been launched. ALMAGUER: As families tighten budgets amid high-interest rates, steep gas prices and rising rents, more than 40 percent of Americans say they aren`t earning enough to cover the cost of holiday gifts this year. PALMER: Basically, retailers know that consumers are really stressed out financially by spreading out those sales over a multi-week, multi-month period. It makes it easier for consumers to keep spending. ALMAGUER: The best advice say experts, do your holiday shopping now and wait for the perfect sale. Last year, 50 percent of shoppers did their holiday shopping before Thanksgiving. Lester? HOLT: All right, Miguel, thanks. Up next, they`re a pivotal group of voters changing the political map. And tonight, the battle over the all-important Latino vote. [19:20:16] (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) TOM LLAMAS, NBC NEWS SENIOR NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): In a state known for hurricanes, in 2020, a political earthquake hit Florida. CHUCK TODD, NBC NEWS POLITICAL DIRECTOR: This Latino thing is an issue here for the Democrats. LLAMAS: Joe Biden won the presidency but Donald Trump took nearly half of the Latino vote in Florida. CARLOS CURBELO , FORMER REPUBLICAN CONGRESSMAN FROM FLORIDA: Republicans figured out how to connect with Latino voters culturally. This is not about policy. LLAMAS: A new NBC News Telemundo poll shows while Latinos lean Democrat and prefer Democratic control of Congress, support for the GOP is up 10 points over five midterm cycles. Congresswoman Maria Elvira Salazar , a daughter of Cuban exiles and former news anchor, flip this district read in 2020. The GOP has made so many gains when it comes to Latinos. headline: Behind The Scenes Of Carrie Underwood`s Epic New Tour
story_text: SHEINELLE JONES: I am excited for this. So, this morning, we have a "TODAY" exclusive. A first look at what to expect when country superstar Carrie Underwood hits the road for her Denim and Rhinestones tour. It`s her first in three years since she took me back stage in South Carolina where it all kicks off. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CARRIE UNDERWOOD, SINGER: It`s a good time. A lot of hard work has gone into the show and very, very proud of it. People are going to have fun. JONES (voiceover): It`s been a few years since a Carrie Underwood tour has made its way across the country. And no one seems more excited than the superstar herself.\\ JONES (on camera): What is the one thing you miss about touring? UNDERWOOD: The crowds. I love to sing. headline: The World-Famous Hollywood Sign Gets A Touch Up Just In Time For A Huge Anniversary
story_text: KRISTEN WELKER: Well, if you`ve ever traveled to Los Angeles, you`ve probably looked high on the Hill to see that world famous Hollywood sign. PETER ALEXANDER: You almost don`t have to travel to Los Angeles to have seen that sign. WELKER: That is right, everywhere. ALEXANDER: It`s like ubiquitous. A big anniversary is approaching for the sign and now it`s getting a pretty nice touch up. NBC`s Steve Patterson grabbed a paintbrush and got to work. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) STEVE PATTERSON, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT (voice over): Every great city has a symbol, representing the ideals of its people. In Hollywood, it`s a sign. Nine giant letters spelling out one iconic notion. This is where dreams are made. Believe it or not, the Hollywood sign is about to turn 100 years old, it was meant to last just 18 months. The sign went up back in 1923 as Hollywoodland, a billboard to sell real estate, but it caught people`s attention and stuck around. In the 40s, it was donated to the city of Los Angeles and the land was removed. JEFF ZARRINNAM, HOLLYWOOD SIGN TRUST CHAIR: The sign came to mean something different. headline: Meet the Press for October 16, 2022, NBC
story_text: [09:00:17] (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) CHUCK TODD, NBC HOST (voice over): This Sunday, the battlegrounds. With the midterms now just 23 days away, the candidates in the Senate races that will determine party control are making their final pitch to voters and facing off on the debate stage, in Georgia... HERSCHEL WALKER , GEORGIA REPUBLICAN SENATE NOMINEE: That was a lie, and I`m not backing down. SEN. RAPHAEL WARNOCK , (D) GEORGIA: My opponent has a problem with the truth. TODD: ... Pennsylvania... MEHMET OZ, PENNSYLVANIA REPUBLICAN SENATE NOMINEE: We should have had a debate already. LT. GOV. JOHN FETTERMAN , (D) PENNSYLVANIA: I actually have a record in fighting crime. TODD: ... and Wisconsin. SEN. RON JOHNSON, (R) WISCONSIN: We have to keep violent criminals in jail. LT. GOV. MANDELA BARNES, (D) WISCONSIN: It is absurd when people say that I`m soft on crime. TODD: I`ll speak with two independents, Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Utah`s independent Senate candidate, Evan McMullin. Plus, Trump`s testimony. REP. BENNIE THOMPSON , (D) MISSISSIPPI & CHAIR, SELECT COMMITTEE ON THE JANUARY 6 ATTACK: He must be accountable. TODD: The January 6th committee issues a subpoena for former President Trump to testify about his role in the attack on the Capitol... REP. LIZ CHENEY, (R) WYOMING & VICE CHAIR, SELECT COMMITTEE ON THE JANUARY 6 ATTACK: We are obligated to seek answers directly from the man who set this all in motion. TODD: ... while new video reveals congressional leaders pleading for help... SEN. CHUCK SCHUMER , (D) NEW YORK & MAJORITY LEADER: Why don`t you get the president to tell them to leave the Capitol? TODD: ... and new questions emerge on how the Secret Service handled advance warnings of the threat. I`ll talk to Democratic congresswoman Stephanie Murphy of Florida, who sits on the committee. And political polarization, why the state of Wisconsin best represents the deep divide playing out in our national politics. My reporting on the ground behind what`s driving the red and blue divisions. (on camera): Joining me for insight and analysis are Amy Walter, editor in chief of the Cook Political Report; Politico "Playbook" co-author Eugene Daniels; former North Carolina Pat McCrory ; and Maria Teresa Kumar, president of Voto Latino. Welcome to Sunday. It`s "Meet the Press." ANNOUNCER: From NBC News in Washington, the longest-running show in television history, this is "Meet the Press With Chuck Todd." TODD: Good Sunday morning. There are just over three weeks to go until Election Day. Nearly 2 million Americans have already voted, just another 120 million to go. So with Republicans still favored to win control of the House, both parties are actually keeping their attention and money right now focused on the battle for control of the Senate, in particular these nine battleground states. These are the nine closest Senate races in the country because they`re trying to keep their top targets in play. In order to win back control, Republicans have to flip one of the Senate seats currently held by the Democrats, Georgia, Arizona, Nevada or New Hampshire, while also holding onto all of their seats that are in play here. Pennsylvania, Ohio, North Carolina are open seats. Florida and Wisconsin feature incumbents. On the Democratic side, Nevada Senator Catherine Cortez Masto is arguably the most vulnerable Democratic incumbent. Republicans are also trying to pick off Georgia Senator Raphael Warnock . But they`ve struggled a bit as allegations about domestic abuse and now abortion seem to saddle Republican Herschel Walker . Georgia now, by the way, has the highest price tag in the country of any mid-term race. More than $140 million has been spent on ads since the primary. By the way, that total is more than what both Bush and Gore spent in the year 2000, if you want to see how much funding has grown exponentially. So the number here will get even bigger, especially if this Georgia race goes into another overtime, as it happened two years ago. This time the runoff would be on December 6th. On Friday night the candidates met in what may be -- may be their only debate, where Walker again denied that he paid for the mother of one of his children to have an abortion. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) WALKER: As I said, that`s a lie. And I said that was a lie, and I`m not backing down. And you have Senator Warnock, people that would do anything and say anything for this seat. But I`m not going to back down because this seat is too important to the Georgia people for me to back down right now. MODERATOR: You`ve been vocally pro-life, supporting a ban on abortions without exceptions. Would you support a complete ban on a national level? Thirty seconds. WALKER: First of all, see, that`s not true, either. I said I support a -- a heartbeat bill, and I said that has exceptions in it. MODERATOR: Do you believe there should be any limitations on abortion set by the government? And you have 60 seconds. WARNOCK: I think that the women of this country and the women of this state woke up one summer morning and a core protection that they`ve known for 50 years was taken from them by an extremist Supreme Court. And I stand where I`ve said I stand in the past, that a patient`s room is too narrow and small and cramped a space for a woman, her doctor and the United States government . (END VIDEOTAPE) TODD: By the way, early voting in Georgia starts tomorrow. Let`s turn now to a few of the Democratic opportunities here. Just two Republican incumbents, as I noted, are in battleground races. [09:05:02] That`s Wisconsin and Florida. But nominees that essentially were hand- picked by Donald Trump in those three open races have made those states more competitive as well. The cycle`s second highest ad price tag is in the state of Pennsylvania. More than $95 million has been spent on ads just since the primary in May. My colleague Dasha Burns had exclusive interviews this week with both Senate nominees. NBC News agreed to Democrat John Fetterman`s request to use a transcription program during the interview because he`s still experiencing some auditory processing issues from a stroke he had in May. Outside, though, of releasing a letter from his cardiologist on June 3rd, the campaign has denied additional requests for his medical records. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) DASHA BURNS, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Don`t voters deserve to know your status now? FETTERMAN: Being on -- in front of thousands and thousands of people and having interviews and getting around all across Pennsylvania, that gives everybody, and the voters decide, you know, if they think that it`s -- it`s really the issue. Dr. Oz likes to make fun of me that I might miss a word, but, you know, he`s missed, you know, two words, and that is "yes" or "no" on the national abortion ban. BURNS: One of your campaign staffers said that John Fetterman wouldn`t have had a stroke if he had, quote, "ever eaten a vegetable in his life." You`re a doctor. You`re a heart doctor. You of all people understand what John Fetterman is going through, better than most. Why would you allow your campaign to mock him like that?
