headline: Today for November 9, 2022, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:00:17] HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good Wednesday morning. After an election night of midterm surprises for both parties. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: And we are still awaiting many of the results. It is November 9th. This is Today. Too close to call key races still to be decided control of Congress hanging in the balance as votes are still being counted in key battlegrounds this morning. In Pennsylvania Democrats pick up a hard fought Senate seat. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) JOHN FETTERMAN (D-PA), SENATOR-ELECT: I`ll be the next U.S. senator from Pennsylvania. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: In Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis wins big, grossing back to the State House and turning Florida decidedly red. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) GOV. RON DESANTIS (R-FL): The people have delivered their verdict. Freedom is here to stay. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: But across the country controversial Republican candidates aligned with former President Trump disappoint. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) SEN. LINDSEY GRAHAM (R-SC): Definitely not a Republican way that`s for darn sure. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: This morning suspense over who will control the House and Senate and the results still rolling in today, Wednesday, November 9th, 2022. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: From NBC News, this is a special edition of Today with Savannah Guthrie and Hoda Kotb live from Studio 1A in Rockefeller Plaza. GUTHRIE: Well, hi, everybody. Good morning and welcome to Today. It is nice to have you with us on a Wednesday morning, the morning after election night. KOTB: One, two, three cups of coffee and one more for you, a long night. But election results by the way, SG, still coming in right now. GUTHRIE: Absolutely. Big night for the NBC News team all-nighters but we still have the question that we headed into the night with, will there be a shift in the balance of power in Congress? It`s unknown at this hour so let`s break it down where things stand, 218 seats are needed to claim majority control in the House. And right now our projection for the House is essentially still a tossup. Now let`s go to the Senate, both parties still neck and neck there as well. KOTB: Yes, Democrats have flipped one seat. NBC News projecting Democrat John Fetterman has won his Pennsylvania seat defeating Dr. Mehmet Oz in a closely watched an extremely expensive race. GUTHRIE: Let`s go down to Georgia, neither Democrat Raphael Warnock or Republican Herschel Walker have met the 50 percent threshold yet necessary to be declared an outright winner. So it could be that they will go to a runoff election in December. KOTB: Yes, it`s still too early to call. The Senate battle in Arizona, that`s between incumbent Senator Mark Kelly and Republican Blake Masters. GUTHRIE: And in Nevada it is just after 4:00 a.m. and we`re starting to see some results in the race between the incumbent Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and Republican challenger Adam Laxalt . So put it this way, we get a lot to get to. Our correspondents, they`ve been up all night they are spread out from coast to coast. Let`s get it started with NBC`s Peter Alexander in Philadelphia this morning. Hi, Peter, good morning. PETER ALEXANDER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Savannah and Hoda, good morning to both of you. What a night. The crucial Senate seat here in Pennsylvania was a top target for both parties. But now the Democrats have secured a huge flip with John Fetterman`s win. Historically in a midterm, the party in power loses dozens of seats. But Democrats this go around defied history and expectations. And with plenty of votes still to be counted, this remains a country that is deeply divided. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) ALEXANDER (voice-over): This morning, controlled of Congress up in the air with both the House and Senate still hanging in the balance. Republicans acknowledging the expected red wave never materialized. GRAHAM: Definitely not a Republican wave that`s for darn sure. SEN. TED CRUZ (R-TX): That hasn`t been as big of a wave as I`d hoped it would be. ALEXANDER (voice-over): While the battle for the Senate may not be decided for days, Democrats are celebrating a critical Senate pick up in Pennsylvania, where Lieutenant Governor John Fetterman just months removed from a stroke, defeated his Republican rival, celebrity T.V., Dr. Mehmet Oz. FETTERMAN: Yes, this campaign has always been about fighting for everyone who`s ever been gotten knocked down that ever got back up. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Georgia`s Senate showdown appears headed to a run off next month if neither incumbent Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock nor Republican Herschel Walker can reach the 50 percent threshold. SEN. RAPHAEL WARNOCK (D-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: You all just hang in there. I`m feeling good. HERSCHEL WALKER (R-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: I told you he`s going to be tough to beat. You got to roll in Georgia here on. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Democrats showed signs of strength in a number of key races. GRAHAM: So you know, you got hats off to the Democrats. They perform well in a lot of these swing districts. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Two Democratic senators who`d been considered vulnerable New Hampshire`s Maggie Hassan and Colorado`s Michael Bennet, both fending off challenges overnight and in some of the country`s most competitive House races Democrats touting narrow victories including in Virginia. [07:05:04] REP. ABIGAIL SPANBERGER (D-VA): Thanks to your commitment and hard work we have won this race. ALEXANDER (voice-over): But some critical wins for the GOP holding on to a key Senate seat in North Carolina. And in Ohio, Republican political novice author J.D. Vance beating Democrat Tim Ryan . Vance was endorsed by former President Trump. J.D. VANCE (R-PA), SENATOR-ELECT: I will never forget where I came from, and I will never forget the great people of Ohio. ALEXANDER (voice-over): A major bright spot for the GOP Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis and Senator Marco Rubio cruising to reelection. Across the country, voters send a message that they`re dissatisfied with President Biden and particularly worried about the economy, with nearly a third saying in exit polls that rising inflation mattered most to them this year, but abortion rights was the second most important issue and a huge motivating factor for Democrats, now both parties facing a deeply divided electorate ahead of the next presidential election. (END VIDEOTAPE) ALEXANDER: And here in Pennsylvania, according to the NBC News exit poll, voters were confident in John Fetterman`s ability to serve this state effectively despite his health challenges. Dr. Mehmet Oz fell short of convincing those same Pennsylvanians that he had lived in this state long enough to serve it. Savannah and Hoda? GUTHRIE: All right, Peter Alexander leading us off. Thank you. KOTB: All right, let`s focus on that closely watched Senate battle in Georgia. It remains too close to call it this hour. NBC`s Gabe Gutierrez spent the night in Atlanta. His watching those results still coming in, have we seen any movement overnight, Gabe? GABE GUTIERREZ, NBC NEWS NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Hoda, good morning. Well, it was a long night here in Georgia. And we`re still at it, no clear winner. And NBC News has not projected this race but a runoff is appearing more and more likely at least that`s according to the Georgia Secretary of State`s office. Now incumbent senator Raphael Warnock is holding that slight lead over his challenger, football legend Herschel Walker . But there`s a third party candidate in this race. And according to Georgia State law, if no candidate reaches that 50 percent threshold, we`ll see a runoff here next month. Now this has been a wild race with more than a quarter billion dollars flowing into the state. And now voters in Georgia are preparing for the possibility of another four weeks of campaigning. Voters I`ve spoken with weren`t too thrilled about that. But in a second race, there was a clear victory. NBC News projects Republican Governor Brian Kemp defeating his Democratic challenger Stacey Abrams for the second time. And the vote tally so far is signaling that at least some Republicans may have voted for Kemp but then voted for the Democrat, Warnock. But again, this Senate race is still too close to call here. And depending on how a few other races go across the country. If we do head to a run off, it could be another several weeks before we know the balance of power in the Senate. Hoda? KOTB: All right, Gabe Gutierrez for us there in Atlanta. Gabe, thank you. GUTHRIE: Let`s go to another pivotal battleground, Arizona, the ballots in that state`s Senate and governor`s race still being counted. NBC`s Vaughn Hillyard is up early in Phoenix. Mark Kelly, the Senate incumbent holds the lead there, but we`re expecting these race results to tighten up. VAUGHN HILLYARD, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Yes, that`s right, Savannah. There are still hundreds of thousands of ballots to be counted here in this race. And it`s going to be challenger Blake Masters who is trying to take down incumbent Democratic Senator Mark Kelly. And you see that he`s down by about six percentage points right now though, but it`s important to note there is as much as one-third of the vote that is still outstanding, and much of that vote is expected to skew toward the GOP. Now election workers are returning here this morning in the Phoenix area to begin signature verifying these mail ballots that were received in recent days. This is going to be a slow process. We should also note the governor`s race, Kari Lake the Republican who is taking on Democratic Katie Hobbs , she well outpacing Masters. She is also losing at this hour to the Democrat. However, overnight, we saw the gap here shrink, and that is what the Republicans are hoping continuous here by weeks and that they are ultimately able to eclipse their Democratic opponent. Savannah? GUTHRIE: All right, Vaughn Hilliard in Arizona. Thank you. KOTB: As we mentioned earlier, we`re still waiting for results out of Nevada`s Senate race too. NBC`s Jacob Soboroff standing by in Vegas, Jacob this race was considered one of the most vulnerable for Democrats. So where do things stand this morning? JACOB SOBOROFF, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: It is still on the line, Hoda. Good morning to you. And Savannah to borrow a line from you last night, what happened in Vegas is going to stay in Vegas, at least for now. It`s not going to Washington, D.C. just quite yet. It was a nail biter out here. That`s what they expected and that is exactly what Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and her Republican challenger, the former state attorney general, Adam Laxalt got. They thought it was going to be a close race. That race is maybe even closer than they thought. Senator Cortes Masto acknowledged as much in a speech to supporters last night. We were there when she told those supporters that this race that hinged on the issues of abortion and the economy is now going to hinge on the pace with which with -- with which, excuse me, those ballots are ultimately going to be counted. And that is because state law here dictates a slow pace of count to ensure a fair and accurate election. [07:10:19] Now the question will be what is Adam Laxalt do? You`ll remember after the 2020 election here, he came out on behalf of President Trump and preemptively challenged the results of the election with baseless conspiracy theory election claims, saying that the election was stolen. That of course was debunked, proven as false by the Republican secretary of state here. Now that he`s in the lead. He took the lead overnight last night. Will he do the same thing? I guess we`ll have to find out today. Meanwhile, the vote count continues out here, guys. KOTB: All right, Jacob Soboroff in Vegas, Jacob, thank you. GUTHRIE: Well, let`s get to our national political correspondent, Steve Kornacki who`s been working the big board throughout the night. He`s back at it this morning. OK. I don`t think 24 hours ago we would have predicted that we wouldn`t know what is going to happen in the House yet. STEVE KORNACKI, NBC NEWS NATIONAL POLITICAL CORRESPONDENT: It`s amazing when you consider Republicans only needed a net gain of five seats to get control of the House. That was the closest a minority party was to winning the House coming into a midterm in nearly a century. And yet this morning, as you say, this is what our NBC News house model is showing. Our projection 218 is what you need to get a majority in the House. Our projection right now is that the Republicans will land at 220 critically plus or minus 10 seats. So in other words, there is very much a universe right now where Republicans could move north of 220 and end up with a majority somewhere around 10 seats or so. There is also a universe where the Democrats could retain control of the House. It remains undecided at this hour. GUTHRIE: And same goes for the Senate. Can we do the same thing on the Senate side? What`s the path to control there for both parties? KORNACKI: Yes, so let`s take a look at it. You heard some reports in the key states there. The big call over night was that Democrats picked up Pennsylvania. That means the Republicans need to gain two Democratic seats if they`re going to get control of the Senate. You see in yellow, what`s uncalled here. Ron Johnson is leading in Wisconsin. Let`s say Ron Johnson holds on to that Republicans would hold that seat. You got the report from Georgia where a runoff is a distinct possibility. Let`s say they do go to a runoff in Georgia, what that would mean is that between Arizona and Nevada, where you just heard those two reports, Republicans would for a moment need to win one of those two, their candidate is trailing in Arizona, their candidate has a lead in Nevada. So between those two, I think the Republicans if they`re going to win one, their prospects are probably better in Nevada than in Arizona. So let`s say the Democrats were to get Arizona, the Republicans were to get Nevada under a scenario like that. This Georgia, the runoff would end up being what decides control of the Senate. That runoff would be held on December 6th. And if the Democrats instead were to sweep Nevada in Arizona, that be it. They control the Senate. GUTHRIE: Well, can we go back to the House for a minute, let`s drill down on what exactly happened and where the Democrats are vulnerable at this hour. We saw what happened in Florida, it was basically a red sweep in Florida. It makes a huge difference for the Republicans. But there`s another place where Democrats are very vulnerable. KORNACKI: This is the surprise. All right, so Democrats have done vastly better than they imagined anyone imagined they would do. And yet look at New York State, right, one of the big blue states. What happened in New York State is the governor`s race, Kathy Hochul , the Democrat gets reelected, but it`s a close race and the Republican Lee Zeldin ran up huge numbers on Long Island and huge numbers upstate. And what that`s done is there`s just a whole bunch of House races in New York State in areas where Zeldin did well, where the Republicans are leading. Look at this one, Sean Patrick Maloney is the chairman of the DCCC, the committee that organizes the Democrats campaign strategy nationally. He is trailing in his own district. Democrats are trailing in two seats on Long Island. Democrats could lose five House seats out of New York. So we`re going through all that math right now, ironically enough, the biggest batch of outstanding results this morning is in New York. And there`s the prospect that Democrats could lose five of them there. That could end up being the difference in the House, New York. GUTHRIE: That`s fascinating to see how this is developing. Steve, thank you very much. Great job. KOTB: Let`s bring in NBC`s senior Washington correspondent Hallie Jackson had a very long night tracking results too. HALLIE JACKSON, NBC NEWS SENIOR WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT: Are you ready for another month of this? KOTB: Well, sounds like it. Let`s talk about what was expected overnight. The polls expected that people were going to vote on inflation and crime that there was going to be a red wave. Yet, a lot of folks probably waking up at this hour going what happened to that red wave? So what did happened? JACKSON: Well, people did vote on inflation and abortion access and crime but it didn`t turn out the way that a lot of people had predicted or thought that it might turn out. As Steve is everybody has laid out here, no, we did not see that red wave materialize. And here`s why that matters, right, let`s say what happens in New York happens as Steve Kornacki has laid out and Republicans do take control of the House of Representatives. The margin matters, right, so whether they got 20 seats, 25 seats, which would be a wave versus like seven matters for a potential future House Speaker, Kevin McCarthy and how governing actually works, whether and how he`s able to wrangle the more far right elements of his caucus to create the laws that affect all of us. [07:15:27] GUTHRIE: Let`s talk about the Trump factor because many analysts are saying it played a role here in terms of the candidates that ran in some states, Trump-backed candidates were chosen in the primary did not perform well last night. Former President Trump out in force in a battleground like Pennsylvania, did that have an effect. JACKSON: Right, before Election Day too. Out in a bunch of battleground states in the four to five days before Election Day, I talked to several Democrats overnight in the wee hours of the morning, this morning, who suggests, yes, the Trump factor is because, why did you -- there all sites, right, I mean, I`ve talked to one PA, Democratic member of Congress, who is surprised happy but surprise. And I said, well, why, like what drove this? And I`ve had Democrats say to me, they do think part of it is the Trump factor here. The fact that when Donald Trump is in the news, Democrats are generally more motivated to come out and vote because it is obviously an anti-Trump vote, it`s not just that he was out in these battleground states like Pennsylvania, it`s that he`s also hinting he may be around for the next couple of years teasing a potential presidential run less than a week from today. KOTB: And just finally, how does the Biden administration feel about what happened overnight? JACKSON: Oh, I think they`re feeling pretty good at this moment. I think because, again, it is not what we expected. Democrats are looking surprisingly strong here today. The question is what does governing look like? I keep coming back to this because that`s what`s going to matter, right? When you look at economy, when you look at inflation, when you look at the potential things that a House, if it is in Republican control can do where does the Senate go? That`s going to be a big impact on how the White House can push anything through as far as a President Biden`s legislative agenda for the next two years. GUTHRIE: All right, Hallie, thank you so much. Catch a nap. There`s much more to talk about. Welcome in Craig, good morning to you. CRAIG MELVIN, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Hey, ladies. Good morning to both of you. To your point there, and good morning to you as well, with results still up in the air, it`s a waiting game in the White House to see what the future holds for President Biden`s agenda. NBC`s chief White House correspondent Kristen Welker joins us now, with more on that part of the story this morning, Kristen, what has been the reaction there so far? KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Craig. Well, good morning. This morning, the president and the White House feeling pretty emboldened this morning after that Republican wave that we`ve been talking about that they feared seemingly never materialized. Now President Biden making calls to winners overnight advisors say, look, while inflation was still clearly a drag on the party, they were especially encouraged that the issue of abortion was a motivating factor for voters. Still you have some Democrats who are worried about their position looking forward to 2024. One of the President`s top allies, in fact, House Majority Whip Jim Clyburn saying overnight Democrats and I`ll read this, Craig, quote, may have to plan for 2024 differently. Does that mean bringing in new people? I don`t know. That`s a quote from Clyburn. But it raises questions about the President`s own future. Now a top Biden adviser telling me this morning nothing has changed about the President`s thinking he has consistently said he intends to run, hasn`t made that final decision yet. We will likely hear more from him about all of this a little bit later on today. Craig? MELVIN: I`m curious quote from Clyburn indeed though. Our chief White House correspondent Kristen Welker for us there, Kristen, thank you. Ladies? GUTHRIE: All right, yes, Craig, we have a lot more results and reaction for you a little bit later. You can find the very latest updates throughout the day on NBC News Daily and of course, tonight on NBC Nightly News. KOTB: And we also are following another major story this morning, a tropical storm, Nicole, bearing down on Florida. Mandatory evacuations have been ordered for parts of its east coast. Dylan is at her post. She`s in for Al once again. Hey, Dylan. DYLAN DREYER, NBC NEWS METEOROLOGIST: Good morning, guys. Yes, let`s start with tropical storm, a potential hurricane into the whole mix here. And we do have still a tropical storm at this time, but it`s very close to being a weak category one hurricane winds. All right, 70 miles per hour right now, it`s moving southwest fairly quickly at 13 mph is going to move through the Bahamas and likely strengthen to a category one hurricane before making landfall tonight into early tomorrow morning just north of West Palm Beach, Florida. Then it tracks across the peninsula here and then takes a turn up towards Tallahassee and then as it rains itself out, it`s going to bring a lot of rain into especially the interior northeast, as the tropical system does. It`s got a lot of water with it. So our biggest concern right now will be for some flash flooding. Also some storm surge flooding right along the east coast of Florida, parts of Florida, north of West Palm Beach, we can see about six to eight inches of rainfall. And then if we extend this up to where the storm is going through the weekend, interior parts of the Northeast could end up with about two to four inches of rain, so a flooding potential even in the Northeast going into the weekend. [07:19:52] That`s a look at the weather across the country. We`ll get to your local forecast in the next 30 seconds. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that`s your latest forecast. KOTB: All right. Thank you, Dylan. We`re also going to check in with Kerry Sanders. He`s alive on Daytona Beach just ahead. GUTHRIE: Plus, we`re going to break down that big night for Florida`s Governor Ron DeSantis , coasting to reelection and perhaps setting the stage for 2024. KOTB: And it`s the $2 billion question in the morning, who bought it? Who bought that winning Powerball ticket? We`ll take you live to a California gas station where it was sold. But first, this is Today on NBC. Oh, my God. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) GUTHRIE: Coming up, I can`t believe I missed this, the new season of "The Crown" made its debut overnight. Keir Simmons catching up with the casts. MELVIN: Yes, well, they want you to know about their take on life inside the royal family after your local news. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:26:21] (LOCAL NEWS) (COMMERCIAL BREAK) (LOCAL NEWS) (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:30:19] KOTB: We`re back now. It is 7:30. It`s a Wednesday morning. It`s November 9th, 2020. All glory outside. MELVIN: Can I just say, I went to sleep with you last night at like 12:00, 12:30. And now this morning -- GUTHRIE: We`re waking up together too. MELVIN: Fresh as a daisy. KOTB: But she only has one, two, three and I`m donating of course here. GUTHRIE: I know. One of these is jet fuel. KOTB: Yes, exactly. MELVIN: Well done. Well done last night. GUTHRIE: Yes, no pints. Not yet. That`s not until 8:40. Let`s get your headlines at 7:30 Wednesday morning. American basketball star Brittney Griner has been moved from a detention center to a Russian penal colony. Last month the Russian court rejected her appeal of that nine year sentence for drug possession. Her legal team says they do not know her exact current location. Russian penal colonies are notorious for overcrowding and harsh conditions. Inmates often subjected to manual labor. KOTB: Breaking overnight, North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile toward its eastern sea this morning, adding to a recent barrage of weapons tests. North Korea fired dozens of missiles last week in reaction to joint military exercises between the United States and South Korea. The North has launched more than 60 ballistic missiles so far this year. MELVIN: A Tyrannosaurus Rex skull unearthed in South Dakota could sell for as much as $20 million at auction next month. The 200 pound fossil nicknamed Maximus is being sold by an owner who wishes to remain anonymous. That skull by the way, it`s about 76 million years old. Experts say despite its age, it`s in remarkable condition. It has most of the external bones and numerous teeth as well. GUTHRIE: It doesn`t look a day over 75 million. MELVIN: SG, what you do with that if you buy it for 20 million? GUTHRIE: I don`t know. KOTB: Let`s turn back to more midterm results and reaction. MELVIN: Yes, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis cruise to victory winning reelection in a landslide over Democrat Charlie Crist . GUTHRIE: His performance cementing his status as a leading figure in the Republican Party boosting his stock as a 2024 presidential contender as well. NBC`s Ali Vitali is in Tampa this morning. She got that part of the midterm story. Hi, Ali, good morning. ALI VITALI, NBC NEWS CAPITOL HILL CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Savannah, good morning. You know, we all know the old Tim Russert mantra. It`s Florida, Florida, Florida. But even on a night like last night where Republicans won by sweeping margins, this state is still in the spotlight seen as more solidly red now than it`s been in years and boosting a new man to the front of the Republican pack. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) VITALI (voice-over): Overnight, a major midterm victory, possibly setting up a preview for the next presidential election. In Florida, Republican Governor Ron DeSantis cruising to reelection in a landslide over Charlie Crist . DESANTIS: I am honored by your support and I look forward to the road ahead. VITALI (voice-over): He`d had a tougher run four years ago winning by less than 1 percent. But Florida is a different state now. He`s projected to flip the key Miami Dade County, the first Republican governor to do so in over a decade. He along with Senator Marco Rubio solidifying GOP control of the one swing state. But DeSantis` victory also cemented his status as a Republican star and a possible front runner for the next presidential election. At his victory rally, the crowd chanting, two more years, signaling support for 2024 run. The Florida governor has made a name for himself in GOP circles over the last few years with his aggressive plans to reopen the state after the COVID pandemic and his fundraising prowess and he`s positioned himself as a key champion of the party, including in a recent ad. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: God looked down on his planned in paradise and said I need to protect her. VITALI (voice-over): All of it catching the attention of former President Donald Trump who has himself teased a 2024 run. Trump technically backing DeSantis but not sparing him, declaring himself the front runner over the weekend. DONALD TRUMP , FORMER PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: There it is Trump at 71 Ron DeSanctimonious at 10 percent. VITALI (voice-over): And previewing serious Republican infighting to come if both do run. GUTHRIE: Let me tell you what President Trump said today to an interview about Ron DeSantis . He said it would be a mistake if DeSantis won one and he said ran for president and he said if he did, Trump said he would say things about him that won`t be flattering, and said I know more about him than anybody. How does this sit with you? GRAHAM: Take it for what it`s worth. Here`s what I think. President Trump if he announces next week, which I think he`s likely to do, we`ll have about six months to himself. VITALI (voice-over): Graham adding that DeSantis has to be governor for a while before getting into the race. Republicans taking a wait and see approach as the popular governor may be gearing up to battle the party`s biggest star. (END VIDEOTAPE) [07:35:04] GUTHRIE: Oh, this could be war, Ali. We already see the rumblings. Are people that you`re talking to voters there who like DeSantis, like Trump? Are they conflicted, torn between these two potential candidates? VITALI: Yes, definitely, Savannah. Look, DeSantis is a popular governor. TRUMP is a popular former president. Voters that I`ve been talking to here over the last few weeks like both of them, many of them don`t want to have to make a choice but it looks like they`re both on a collision course. I really saw it last night as I was leaving the DeSantis event, a man came up to me wearing a Make America Great Again hat, unfurling a Trump 2024 banner. He said he hoped that Trump could run in 2024. And that DeSantis could wait until 2028. I don`t want to count that far ahead into the future. But it`s clear that voter`s minds are already there. And frankly, in my text with Republican donors, their minds are already there, too. They`re starting to make some early picks as the shadow primary becomes a lot more public now. GUTHRIE: All right, Ali, thank you so much. That`s the worst thing about the day after the midterms. They start talking about the next election. We can`t talk about 2028, no. KOTB: We need a minute here. GUTHRIE: Yes. KOTB: All right, guys, still ahead, the mystery and drama surrounding that record shattering Powerball jackpot. We are live at that gas station near L.A. where the winning ticket was sold, a single ticket after that hours long delay in the drawing. MELVIN: Hard to believe that. We`re also going to go back to Florida as well because millions in storm weary Florida are once again bracing for a possible hurricane in November. And it could strike as soon as tonight. We`re going to have a live report from Kerry Sanders and we`ll get Dylan`s forecast right after this. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:41:11] GUTHRIE: All right, we`re back. Let`s dig into it that record breaking Powerball drawing. There was the hours long mysterious delay and then somebody won. KOTB: That was totally weird. Well, it all came down to one single winning ticket it was sold. It was worth more than $2 billion. MELVIN: Yes. Dana Griffin clearly didn`t win because she is outside that store in Los Angeles, where the boarding ticket was purchased. Hey, Dana, good morning. DANA GRIFFIN, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Craig, good morning to you and everyone else. You know, after three months and a processing delay, we finally have a Powerball winner, the biggest in history. That $2 billion ticket was sold here at Joe Service Center in Altadena. The big question now, who has it? (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) GRIFFIN (voice-over): After 40 straight winless drawings, someone is taking home the largest lottery prize in history. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: This is Powerball. GRIFFIN (voice-over): This morning, one person is holding the only ticket matching all six winning Powerball numbers, the jackpot reaching $2,040,000,000 a lump sum payout will be more than 997 million before taxes. CAROLYN BECKER, CALIFORNIA LOTTERY SPOKESPERSON: Joe Service Center had the privilege of selling the only Powerball jackpot winning ticket. GRIFFIN (voice-over): That ticket sold just outside of Los Angeles at this gas station in Altadena, California. The jackpot so massive, lottery officials had to take the letter B on the winning billionaire banner. BECKER: We never had to do this. GRIFFIN (voice-over): The historic win came after a technical issue in Minnesota calls the drawing to experience a 10-hour delay. Now the lucky player is California lottery`s first ever billionaire. (on camera): The big question, who won? BECKER: It is the billion dollar question. The $2 billion question we don`t know who won. GRIFFIN (voice-over): No one has claimed the big prize yet, the winner won`t stay a mystery forever. California law requires their name to eventually be made public. Still, the advice from lottery experts lay low before claiming the record breaking payout. KURT PANOUSES, TAX ATTORNEY AND CPA: They need to take their time. They need to slow down. And as I always tell people, wait for the roller coaster to come to a stop before you try to get off. GRIFFIN (voice-over): But the newest billionaire won`t be the only one cashing in. More than 11 million tickets won something with cash prizes totaling $98 million including 3 more million dollar winners in the Golden State. The jackpot selling store`s owner Joseph Chahayed will also enjoy a million dollar bonus as we all wait for someone to claim that historic grand prize (on camera): What do you want to tell that person who is probably sitting at home trying to wrap his or her head? JOSEPH CHAHAYED, GAS STATION OWNER: I love you before and I love you know and I`m going to love you forever. (END VIDEOTAPE) GRIFFIN: So Papa Joe as he`s known around here is definitely filling that lottery love this morning. Now the winner has up to a year to claim that ticket. And if you weren`t the lucky winner, no worries. Guess what? There`s going to be another Powerball drawing tonight. Just a little smaller prize at $20 million, guys. MELVIN: All right, Dana Griffin, Dana, welcome to NBC News by the way. KOTB: Way to go, Dana. MELVIN: Welcome to the Peacock. KOTB: You did great report. GRIFFIN: Thank you. Thank you. Happy to be here. KOTB: All right. GUTHRIE: We won the lottery with her. MELVIN: There you go. Welcome to NBC. Let`s turn now to the latest on the new hurricane threat facing Florida this morning. KOTB: Yes, six weeks after and now Nicole taking aim at the state expected to gain strength before making landfall. We`re going to get to Dylan`s forecast in just a moment. But first, NBC`s Kerry Sanders he joins us from Daytona Beach shores. Hey, Kerry, good morning. KERRY SANDERS, NBC NEWS SENIOR NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Good morning guys. Look, you can see the Atlantic Ocean over my shoulder. It`s kicking up. The winds are picking up. The commercial airports in the area, that`s Orlando, Daytona Beach, Melbourne, they`re either closed or will be closing because of the approaching Tropical Storm that may become a Hurricane Nicole. [07:45:02] The big threat of course here is along the coast coastal erosion. And as you take a look at some of these pictures just leading into the arrival of Nicole, you`ll get a better understanding as to why Ian hammered this area and a lot of the coast was lost to the storm at the same time with the winds coming in. We have the threat to Artemis. OK. That rocket right now is sitting on the pad. It was supposed to launch on the 14th it`s now been pushed back to the 16th. It`s designed to withstand winds of about 85 miles per hour. But the real threat is going to be the rain. So NASA has put out staff to triple check all the hatches to make sure that everything is sealed. Meantime, mandatory evacuations from Flagler County all the way down to Martin County. Those who live in coastal Zone A have been told to leave. And as you saw from those pictures, the biggest threat of course with the coastal erosion is some of the buildings it`s feared by officials could actually have their foundations undermined and they could collapse. So a lot of attention anybody in a mobile home told also to go inland to shelters and then ultimately, tourists in the area who might be caught off guard, they should also find out where those shelters are. They`re open to everybody not just residents, guys. KOTB: Yes, good advice. Kerry Sanders for us there. Kerry, thank you. GUTHRIE: OK, let`s go to Dylan. She`s got the very latest on Nicole, the rest of today`s forecast in for Al this morning, hey. DREYER: Good morning again, guys. And I want to point out that hurricanes hitting the United States in November is pretty rare. We`ve only ever had it happen three times. So this would be the fourth one if this does strengthen into a category one storm. It is still a tropical storm, but it`s very close to being a weak category one so that`s why we do have your hurricane warnings in effect and it`s just north of West Palm Beach where we`re expecting landfall tonight, into tomorrow morning around 10:00 p.m. to about 2:00 a.m. tomorrow morning. And as this makes its way on shore, we are going to see that push of water. The good thing is it`s low tide when the storm is expected to make landfall but still on the backside of that your next high tide about six hours later, we could end up with a three to five foot storm surge. And we`re also looking for that to make its way up into the Northeast. Rainfall totals about eight inches possible in parts of Florida in the Northeast. We can see about two to four inches of rain. That`s a look at the weather across the country. Now here`s a peek out your window. (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that`s your latest forecast. [07:48:03] KOTB: All right, Dylan, thank you. Still ahead, our exclusive look at a new and emotional interview with Jennifer Aniston she`s opening up about the public scrutiny that surrounds her private life and her secret struggles with fertility. CARSON DALY, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good morning everybody. Good to see you. Coming up on PopStart. Jen on Jen, we got the very sweet message that J.Lo was sharing about her husband`s former wife. headline: Today for November 9, 2022, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:00:17] HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good Wednesday morning. After an election night of midterm surprises for both parties. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: And we are still awaiting many of the results. It is November 9th. This is Today. Too close to call key races still to be decided control of Congress hanging in the balance as votes are still being counted in key battlegrounds this morning. In Pennsylvania Democrats pick up a hard fought Senate seat. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) JOHN FETTERMAN (D-PA), SENATOR-ELECT: I`ll be the next U.S. senator from Pennsylvania. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: In Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis wins big, grossing back to the State House and turning Florida decidedly red. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) GOV. RON DESANTIS (R-FL): The people have delivered their verdict. Freedom is here to stay. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: But across the country controversial Republican candidates aligned with former President Trump disappoint. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) SEN. LINDSEY GRAHAM (R-SC): Definitely not a Republican way that`s for darn sure. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: This morning suspense over who will control the House and Senate and the results still rolling in today, Wednesday, November 9th, 2022. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: From NBC News, this is a special edition of Today with Savannah Guthrie and Hoda Kotb live from Studio 1A in Rockefeller Plaza. GUTHRIE: Well, hi, everybody. Good morning and welcome to Today. It is nice to have you with us on a Wednesday morning, the morning after election night. KOTB: One, two, three cups of coffee and one more for you, a long night. But election results by the way, SG, still coming in right now. GUTHRIE: Absolutely. Big night for the NBC News team all-nighters but we still have the question that we headed into the night with, will there be a shift in the balance of power in Congress? It`s unknown at this hour so let`s break it down where things stand, 218 seats are needed to claim majority control in the House. And right now our projection for the House is essentially still a tossup. Now let`s go to the Senate, both parties still neck and neck there as well. KOTB: Yes, Democrats have flipped one seat. NBC News projecting Democrat John Fetterman has won his Pennsylvania seat defeating Dr. Mehmet Oz in a closely watched an extremely expensive race. GUTHRIE: Let`s go down to Georgia, neither Democrat Raphael Warnock or Republican Herschel Walker have met the 50 percent threshold yet necessary to be declared an outright winner. So it could be that they will go to a runoff election in December. KOTB: Yes, it`s still too early to call. The Senate battle in Arizona, that`s between incumbent Senator Mark Kelly and Republican Blake Masters. GUTHRIE: And in Nevada it is just after 4:00 a.m. and we`re starting to see some results in the race between the incumbent Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and Republican challenger Adam Laxalt . So put it this way, we get a lot to get to. Our correspondents, they`ve been up all night they are spread out from coast to coast. Let`s get it started with NBC`s Peter Alexander in Philadelphia this morning. Hi, Peter, good morning. PETER ALEXANDER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Savannah and Hoda, good morning to both of you. What a night. The crucial Senate seat here in Pennsylvania was a top target for both parties. But now the Democrats have secured a huge flip with John Fetterman`s win. Historically in a midterm, the party in power loses dozens of seats. But Democrats this go around defied history and expectations. And with plenty of votes still to be counted, this remains a country that is deeply divided. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) ALEXANDER (voice-over): This morning, controlled of Congress up in the air with both the House and Senate still hanging in the balance. Republicans acknowledging the expected red wave never materialized. GRAHAM: Definitely not a Republican wave that`s for darn sure. SEN. TED CRUZ (R-TX): That hasn`t been as big of a wave as I`d hoped it would be. ALEXANDER (voice-over): While the battle for the Senate may not be decided for days, Democrats are celebrating a critical Senate pick up in Pennsylvania, where Lieutenant Governor John Fetterman just months removed from a stroke, defeated his Republican rival, celebrity T.V., Dr. Mehmet Oz. FETTERMAN: Yes, this campaign has always been about fighting for everyone who`s ever been gotten knocked down that ever got back up. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Georgia`s Senate showdown appears headed to a run off next month if neither incumbent Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock nor Republican Herschel Walker can reach the 50 percent threshold. SEN. RAPHAEL WARNOCK (D-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: You all just hang in there. I`m feeling good. HERSCHEL WALKER (R-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: I told you he`s going to be tough to beat. You got to roll in Georgia here on. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Democrats showed signs of strength in a number of key races. GRAHAM: So you know, you got hats off to the Democrats. They perform well in a lot of these swing districts. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Two Democratic senators who`d been considered vulnerable New Hampshire`s Maggie Hassan and Colorado`s Michael Bennet, both fending off challenges overnight and in some of the country`s most competitive House races Democrats touting narrow victories including in Virginia. [07:05:04] REP. ABIGAIL SPANBERGER (D-VA): Thanks to your commitment and hard work we have won this race. ALEXANDER (voice-over): But some critical wins for the GOP holding on to a key Senate seat in North Carolina. And in Ohio, Republican political novice author J.D. Vance beating Democrat Tim Ryan . Vance was endorsed by former President Trump. J.D. VANCE (R-PA), SENATOR-ELECT: I will never forget where I came from, and I will never forget the great people of Ohio. ALEXANDER (voice-over): A major bright spot for the GOP Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis and Senator Marco Rubio cruising to reelection. Across the country, voters send a message that they`re dissatisfied with President Biden and particularly worried about the economy, with nearly a third saying in exit polls that rising inflation mattered most to them this year, but abortion rights was the second most important issue and a huge motivating factor for Democrats, now both parties facing a deeply divided electorate ahead of the next presidential election. (END VIDEOTAPE) ALEXANDER: And here in Pennsylvania, according to the NBC News exit poll, voters were confident in John Fetterman`s ability to serve this state effectively despite his health challenges. Dr. Mehmet Oz fell short of convincing those same Pennsylvanians that he had lived in this state long enough to serve it. Savannah and Hoda? GUTHRIE: All right, Peter Alexander leading us off. Thank you. KOTB: All right, let`s focus on that closely watched Senate battle in Georgia. It remains too close to call it this hour. NBC`s Gabe Gutierrez spent the night in Atlanta. His watching those results still coming in, have we seen any movement overnight, Gabe? GABE GUTIERREZ, NBC NEWS NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Hoda, good morning. Well, it was a long night here in Georgia. And we`re still at it, no clear winner. And NBC News has not projected this race but a runoff is appearing more and more likely at least that`s according to the Georgia Secretary of State`s office. Now incumbent senator Raphael Warnock is holding that slight lead over his challenger, football legend Herschel Walker . But there`s a third party candidate in this race. And according to Georgia State law, if no candidate reaches that 50 percent threshold, we`ll see a runoff here next month. Now this has been a wild race with more than a quarter billion dollars flowing into the state. And now voters in Georgia are preparing for the possibility of another four weeks of campaigning. Voters I`ve spoken with weren`t too thrilled about that. But in a second race, there was a clear victory. NBC News projects Republican Governor Brian Kemp defeating his Democratic challenger Stacey Abrams for the second time. And the vote tally so far is signaling that at least some Republicans may have voted for Kemp but then voted for the Democrat, Warnock. But again, this Senate race is still too close to call here. And depending on how a few other races go across the country. If we do head to a run off, it could be another several weeks before we know the balance of power in the Senate. Hoda? KOTB: All right, Gabe Gutierrez for us there in Atlanta. Gabe, thank you. GUTHRIE: Let`s go to another pivotal battleground, Arizona, the ballots in that state`s Senate and governor`s race still being counted. NBC`s Vaughn Hillyard is up early in Phoenix. Mark Kelly, the Senate incumbent holds the lead there, but we`re expecting these race results to tighten up. VAUGHN HILLYARD, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Yes, that`s right, Savannah. There are still hundreds of thousands of ballots to be counted here in this race. And it`s going to be challenger Blake Masters who is trying to take down incumbent Democratic Senator Mark Kelly. And you see that he`s down by about six percentage points right now though, but it`s important to note there is as much as one-third of the vote that is still outstanding, and much of that vote is expected to skew toward the GOP. Now election workers are returning here this morning in the Phoenix area to begin signature verifying these mail ballots that were received in recent days. This is going to be a slow process. We should also note the governor`s race, Kari Lake the Republican who is taking on Democratic Katie Hobbs , she well outpacing Masters. She is also losing at this hour to the Democrat. However, overnight, we saw the gap here shrink, and that is what the Republicans are hoping continuous here by weeks and that they are ultimately able to eclipse their Democratic opponent. Savannah? GUTHRIE: All right, Vaughn Hilliard in Arizona. Thank you. KOTB: As we mentioned earlier, we`re still waiting for results out of Nevada`s Senate race too. NBC`s Jacob Soboroff standing by in Vegas, Jacob this race was considered one of the most vulnerable for Democrats. So where do things stand this morning? JACOB SOBOROFF, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: It is still on the line, Hoda. Good morning to you. And Savannah to borrow a line from you last night, what happened in Vegas is going to stay in Vegas, at least for now. It`s not going to Washington, D.C. just quite yet. It was a nail biter out here. That`s what they expected and that is exactly what Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and her Republican challenger, the former state attorney general, Adam Laxalt got. They thought it was going to be a close race. That race is maybe even closer than they thought. Senator Cortes Masto acknowledged as much in a speech to supporters last night. We were there when she told those supporters that this race that hinged on the issues of abortion and the economy is now going to hinge on the pace with which with -- with which, excuse me, those ballots are ultimately going to be counted. And that is because state law here dictates a slow pace of count to ensure a fair and accurate election. [07:10:19] Now the question will be what is Adam Laxalt do? You`ll remember after the 2020 election here, he came out on behalf of President Trump and preemptively challenged the results of the election with baseless conspiracy theory election claims, saying that the election was stolen. That of course was debunked, proven as false by the Republican secretary of state here. Now that he`s in the lead. He took the lead overnight last night. Will he do the same thing? I guess we`ll have to find out today. Meanwhile, the vote count continues out here, guys. KOTB: All right, Jacob Soboroff in Vegas, Jacob, thank you. GUTHRIE: Well, let`s get to our national political correspondent, Steve Kornacki who`s been working the big board throughout the night. He`s back at it this morning. OK. I don`t think 24 hours ago we would have predicted that we wouldn`t know what is going to happen in the House yet. STEVE KORNACKI, NBC NEWS NATIONAL POLITICAL CORRESPONDENT: It`s amazing when you consider Republicans only needed a net gain of five seats to get control of the House. That was the closest a minority party was to winning the House coming into a midterm in nearly a century. And yet this morning, as you say, this is what our NBC News house model is showing. Our projection 218 is what you need to get a majority in the House. Our projection right now is that the Republicans will land at 220 critically plus or minus 10 seats. So in other words, there is very much a universe right now where Republicans could move north of 220 and end up with a majority somewhere around 10 seats or so. There is also a universe where the Democrats could retain control of the House. It remains undecided at this hour. GUTHRIE: And same goes for the Senate. Can we do the same thing on the Senate side? What`s the path to control there for both parties? KORNACKI: Yes, so let`s take a look at it. You heard some reports in the key states there. The big call over night was that Democrats picked up Pennsylvania. That means the Republicans need to gain two Democratic seats if they`re going to get control of the Senate. You see in yellow, what`s uncalled here. Ron Johnson is leading in Wisconsin. Let`s say Ron Johnson holds on to that Republicans would hold that seat. You got the report from Georgia where a runoff is a distinct possibility. Let`s say they do go to a runoff in Georgia, what that would mean is that between Arizona and Nevada, where you just heard those two reports, Republicans would for a moment need to win one of those two, their candidate is trailing in Arizona, their candidate has a lead in Nevada. So between those two, I think the Republicans if they`re going to win one, their prospects are probably better in Nevada than in Arizona. So let`s say the Democrats were to get Arizona, the Republicans were to get Nevada under a scenario like that. This Georgia, the runoff would end up being what decides control of the Senate. That runoff would be held on December 6th. And if the Democrats instead were to sweep Nevada in Arizona, that be it. They control the Senate. GUTHRIE: Well, can we go back to the House for a minute, let`s drill down on what exactly happened and where the Democrats are vulnerable at this hour. We saw what happened in Florida, it was basically a red sweep in Florida. It makes a huge difference for the Republicans. But there`s another place where Democrats are very vulnerable. KORNACKI: This is the surprise. All right, so Democrats have done vastly better than they imagined anyone imagined they would do. And yet look at New York State, right, one of the big blue states. What happened in New York State is the governor`s race, Kathy Hochul , the Democrat gets reelected, but it`s a close race and the Republican Lee Zeldin ran up huge numbers on Long Island and huge numbers upstate. And what that`s done is there`s just a whole bunch of House races in New York State in areas where Zeldin did well, where the Republicans are leading. Look at this one, Sean Patrick Maloney is the chairman of the DCCC, the committee that organizes the Democrats campaign strategy nationally. He is trailing in his own district. Democrats are trailing in two seats on Long Island. Democrats could lose five House seats out of New York. So we`re going through all that math right now, ironically enough, the biggest batch of outstanding results this morning is in New York. And there`s the prospect that Democrats could lose five of them there. That could end up being the difference in the House, New York. GUTHRIE: That`s fascinating to see how this is developing. Steve, thank you very much. Great job. KOTB: Let`s bring in NBC`s senior Washington correspondent Hallie Jackson had a very long night tracking results too. HALLIE JACKSON, NBC NEWS SENIOR WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT: Are you ready for another month of this? KOTB: Well, sounds like it. Let`s talk about what was expected overnight. The polls expected that people were going to vote on inflation and crime that there was going to be a red wave. Yet, a lot of folks probably waking up at this hour going what happened to that red wave? So what did happened? JACKSON: Well, people did vote on inflation and abortion access and crime but it didn`t turn out the way that a lot of people had predicted or thought that it might turn out. As Steve is everybody has laid out here, no, we did not see that red wave materialize. And here`s why that matters, right, let`s say what happens in New York happens as Steve Kornacki has laid out and Republicans do take control of the House of Representatives. The margin matters, right, so whether they got 20 seats, 25 seats, which would be a wave versus like seven matters for a potential future House Speaker, Kevin McCarthy and how governing actually works, whether and how he`s able to wrangle the more far right elements of his caucus to create the laws that affect all of us. [07:15:27] GUTHRIE: Let`s talk about the Trump factor because many analysts are saying it played a role here in terms of the candidates that ran in some states, Trump-backed candidates were chosen in the primary did not perform well last night. Former President Trump out in force in a battleground like Pennsylvania, did that have an effect. JACKSON: Right, before Election Day too. Out in a bunch of battleground states in the four to five days before Election Day, I talked to several Democrats overnight in the wee hours of the morning, this morning, who suggests, yes, the Trump factor is because, why did you -- there all sites, right, I mean, I`ve talked to one PA, Democratic member of Congress, who is surprised happy but surprise. And I said, well, why, like what drove this? And I`ve had Democrats say to me, they do think part of it is the Trump factor here. The fact that when Donald Trump is in the news, Democrats are generally more motivated to come out and vote because it is obviously an anti-Trump vote, it`s not just that he was out in these battleground states like Pennsylvania, it`s that he`s also hinting he may be around for the next couple of years teasing a potential presidential run less than a week from today. KOTB: And just finally, how does the Biden administration feel about what happened overnight? JACKSON: Oh, I think they`re feeling pretty good at this moment. I think because, again, it is not what we expected. Democrats are looking surprisingly strong here today. The question is what does governing look like? I keep coming back to this because that`s what`s going to matter, right? When you look at economy, when you look at inflation, when you look at the potential things that a House, if it is in Republican control can do where does the Senate go? That`s going to be a big impact on how the White House can push anything through as far as a President Biden`s legislative agenda for the next two years. GUTHRIE: All right, Hallie, thank you so much. Catch a nap. There`s much more to talk about. Welcome in Craig, good morning to you. CRAIG MELVIN, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Hey, ladies. Good morning to both of you. To your point there, and good morning to you as well, with results still up in the air, it`s a waiting game in the White House to see what the future holds for President Biden`s agenda. NBC`s chief White House correspondent Kristen Welker joins us now, with more on that part of the story this morning, Kristen, what has been the reaction there so far? KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Craig. Well, good morning. This morning, the president and the White House feeling pretty emboldened this morning after that Republican wave that we`ve been talking about that they feared seemingly never materialized. Now President Biden making calls to winners overnight advisors say, look, while inflation was still clearly a drag on the party, they were especially encouraged that the issue of abortion was a motivating factor for voters. Still you have some Democrats who are worried about their position looking forward to 2024. One of the President`s top allies, in fact, House Majority Whip Jim Clyburn saying overnight Democrats and I`ll read this, Craig, quote, may have to plan for 2024 differently. Does that mean bringing in new people? I don`t know. That`s a quote from Clyburn. But it raises questions about the President`s own future. Now a top Biden adviser telling me this morning nothing has changed about the President`s thinking he has consistently said he intends to run, hasn`t made that final decision yet. We will likely hear more from him about all of this a little bit later on today. Craig? MELVIN: I`m curious quote from Clyburn indeed though. Our chief White House correspondent Kristen Welker for us there, Kristen, thank you. Ladies? GUTHRIE: All right, yes, Craig, we have a lot more results and reaction for you a little bit later. You can find the very latest updates throughout the day on NBC News Daily and of course, tonight on NBC Nightly News. KOTB: And we also are following another major story this morning, a tropical storm, Nicole, bearing down on Florida. Mandatory evacuations have been ordered for parts of its east coast. Dylan is at her post. She`s in for Al once again. Hey, Dylan. DYLAN DREYER, NBC NEWS METEOROLOGIST: Good morning, guys. Yes, let`s start with tropical storm, a potential hurricane into the whole mix here. And we do have still a tropical storm at this time, but it`s very close to being a weak category one hurricane winds. All right, 70 miles per hour right now, it`s moving southwest fairly quickly at 13 mph is going to move through the Bahamas and likely strengthen to a category one hurricane before making landfall tonight into early tomorrow morning just north of West Palm Beach, Florida. Then it tracks across the peninsula here and then takes a turn up towards Tallahassee and then as it rains itself out, it`s going to bring a lot of rain into especially the interior northeast, as the tropical system does. It`s got a lot of water with it. So our biggest concern right now will be for some flash flooding. Also some storm surge flooding right along the east coast of Florida, parts of Florida, north of West Palm Beach, we can see about six to eight inches of rainfall. And then if we extend this up to where the storm is going through the weekend, interior parts of the Northeast could end up with about two to four inches of rain, so a flooding potential even in the Northeast going into the weekend. [07:19:52] That`s a look at the weather across the country. We`ll get to your local forecast in the next 30 seconds. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that`s your latest forecast. KOTB: All right. Thank you, Dylan. We`re also going to check in with Kerry Sanders. He`s alive on Daytona Beach just ahead. GUTHRIE: Plus, we`re going to break down that big night for Florida`s Governor Ron DeSantis , coasting to reelection and perhaps setting the stage for 2024. KOTB: And it`s the $2 billion question in the morning, who bought it? Who bought that winning Powerball ticket? We`ll take you live to a California gas station where it was sold. But first, this is Today on NBC. Oh, my God. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) GUTHRIE: Coming up, I can`t believe I missed this, the new season of "The Crown" made its debut overnight. Keir Simmons catching up with the casts. MELVIN: Yes, well, they want you to know about their take on life inside the royal family after your local news. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:26:21] (LOCAL NEWS) (COMMERCIAL BREAK) (LOCAL NEWS) (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:30:19] KOTB: We`re back now. It is 7:30. It`s a Wednesday morning. It`s November 9th, 2020. All glory outside. MELVIN: Can I just say, I went to sleep with you last night at like 12:00, 12:30. And now this morning -- GUTHRIE: We`re waking up together too. MELVIN: Fresh as a daisy. KOTB: But she only has one, two, three and I`m donating of course here. GUTHRIE: I know. One of these is jet fuel. KOTB: Yes, exactly. MELVIN: Well done. Well done last night. GUTHRIE: Yes, no pints. Not yet. That`s not until 8:40. Let`s get your headlines at 7:30 Wednesday morning. American basketball star Brittney Griner has been moved from a detention center to a Russian penal colony. Last month the Russian court rejected her appeal of that nine year sentence for drug possession. Her legal team says they do not know her exact current location. Russian penal colonies are notorious for overcrowding and harsh conditions. Inmates often subjected to manual labor. KOTB: Breaking overnight, North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile toward its eastern sea this morning, adding to a recent barrage of weapons tests. North Korea fired dozens of missiles last week in reaction to joint military exercises between the United States and South Korea. The North has launched more than 60 ballistic missiles so far this year. MELVIN: A Tyrannosaurus Rex skull unearthed in South Dakota could sell for as much as $20 million at auction next month. The 200 pound fossil nicknamed Maximus is being sold by an owner who wishes to remain anonymous. That skull by the way, it`s about 76 million years old. Experts say despite its age, it`s in remarkable condition. It has most of the external bones and numerous teeth as well. GUTHRIE: It doesn`t look a day over 75 million. MELVIN: SG, what you do with that if you buy it for 20 million? GUTHRIE: I don`t know. KOTB: Let`s turn back to more midterm results and reaction. MELVIN: Yes, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis cruise to victory winning reelection in a landslide over Democrat Charlie Crist . GUTHRIE: His performance cementing his status as a leading figure in the Republican Party boosting his stock as a 2024 presidential contender as well. NBC`s Ali Vitali is in Tampa this morning. She got that part of the midterm story. Hi, Ali, good morning. ALI VITALI, NBC NEWS CAPITOL HILL CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Savannah, good morning. You know, we all know the old Tim Russert mantra. It`s Florida, Florida, Florida. But even on a night like last night where Republicans won by sweeping margins, this state is still in the spotlight seen as more solidly red now than it`s been in years and boosting a new man to the front of the Republican pack. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) VITALI (voice-over): Overnight, a major midterm victory, possibly setting up a preview for the next presidential election. In Florida, Republican Governor Ron DeSantis cruising to reelection in a landslide over Charlie Crist . DESANTIS: I am honored by your support and I look forward to the road ahead. VITALI (voice-over): He`d had a tougher run four years ago winning by less than 1 percent. But Florida is a different state now. He`s projected to flip the key Miami Dade County, the first Republican governor to do so in over a decade. He along with Senator Marco Rubio solidifying GOP control of the one swing state. But DeSantis` victory also cemented his status as a Republican star and a possible front runner for the next presidential election. At his victory rally, the crowd chanting, two more years, signaling support for 2024 run. The Florida governor has made a name for himself in GOP circles over the last few years with his aggressive plans to reopen the state after the COVID pandemic and his fundraising prowess and he`s positioned himself as a key champion of the party, including in a recent ad. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: God looked down on his planned in paradise and said I need to protect her. VITALI (voice-over): All of it catching the attention of former President Donald Trump who has himself teased a 2024 run. Trump technically backing DeSantis but not sparing him, declaring himself the front runner over the weekend. DONALD TRUMP , FORMER PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: There it is Trump at 71 Ron DeSanctimonious at 10 percent. VITALI (voice-over): And previewing serious Republican infighting to come if both do run. GUTHRIE: Let me tell you what President Trump said today to an interview about Ron DeSantis . He said it would be a mistake if DeSantis won one and he said ran for president and he said if he did, Trump said he would say things about him that won`t be flattering, and said I know more about him than anybody. How does this sit with you? GRAHAM: Take it for what it`s worth. Here`s what I think. President Trump if he announces next week, which I think he`s likely to do, we`ll have about six months to himself. VITALI (voice-over): Graham adding that DeSantis has to be governor for a while before getting into the race. Republicans taking a wait and see approach as the popular governor may be gearing up to battle the party`s biggest star. (END VIDEOTAPE) [07:35:04] GUTHRIE: Oh, this could be war, Ali. We already see the rumblings. Are people that you`re talking to voters there who like DeSantis, like Trump? Are they conflicted, torn between these two potential candidates? VITALI: Yes, definitely, Savannah. Look, DeSantis is a popular governor. TRUMP is a popular former president. Voters that I`ve been talking to here over the last few weeks like both of them, many of them don`t want to have to make a choice but it looks like they`re both on a collision course. I really saw it last night as I was leaving the DeSantis event, a man came up to me wearing a Make America Great Again hat, unfurling a Trump 2024 banner. He said he hoped that Trump could run in 2024. And that DeSantis could wait until 2028. I don`t want to count that far ahead into the future. But it`s clear that voter`s minds are already there. And frankly, in my text with Republican donors, their minds are already there, too. They`re starting to make some early picks as the shadow primary becomes a lot more public now. GUTHRIE: All right, Ali, thank you so much. That`s the worst thing about the day after the midterms. They start talking about the next election. We can`t talk about 2028, no. KOTB: We need a minute here. GUTHRIE: Yes. KOTB: All right, guys, still ahead, the mystery and drama surrounding that record shattering Powerball jackpot. We are live at that gas station near L.A. where the winning ticket was sold, a single ticket after that hours long delay in the drawing. MELVIN: Hard to believe that. We`re also going to go back to Florida as well because millions in storm weary Florida are once again bracing for a possible hurricane in November. And it could strike as soon as tonight. We`re going to have a live report from Kerry Sanders and we`ll get Dylan`s forecast right after this. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:41:11] GUTHRIE: All right, we`re back. Let`s dig into it that record breaking Powerball drawing. There was the hours long mysterious delay and then somebody won. KOTB: That was totally weird. Well, it all came down to one single winning ticket it was sold. It was worth more than $2 billion. MELVIN: Yes. Dana Griffin clearly didn`t win because she is outside that store in Los Angeles, where the boarding ticket was purchased. Hey, Dana, good morning. DANA GRIFFIN, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Craig, good morning to you and everyone else. You know, after three months and a processing delay, we finally have a Powerball winner, the biggest in history. That $2 billion ticket was sold here at Joe Service Center in Altadena. The big question now, who has it? (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) GRIFFIN (voice-over): After 40 straight winless drawings, someone is taking home the largest lottery prize in history. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: This is Powerball. GRIFFIN (voice-over): This morning, one person is holding the only ticket matching all six winning Powerball numbers, the jackpot reaching $2,040,000,000 a lump sum payout will be more than 997 million before taxes. CAROLYN BECKER, CALIFORNIA LOTTERY SPOKESPERSON: Joe Service Center had the privilege of selling the only Powerball jackpot winning ticket. GRIFFIN (voice-over): That ticket sold just outside of Los Angeles at this gas station in Altadena, California. The jackpot so massive, lottery officials had to take the letter B on the winning billionaire banner. BECKER: We never had to do this. GRIFFIN (voice-over): The historic win came after a technical issue in Minnesota calls the drawing to experience a 10-hour delay. Now the lucky player is California lottery`s first ever billionaire. (on camera): The big question, who won? BECKER: It is the billion dollar question. The $2 billion question we don`t know who won. GRIFFIN (voice-over): No one has claimed the big prize yet, the winner won`t stay a mystery forever. California law requires their name to eventually be made public. Still, the advice from lottery experts lay low before claiming the record breaking payout. KURT PANOUSES, TAX ATTORNEY AND CPA: They need to take their time. They need to slow down. And as I always tell people, wait for the roller coaster to come to a stop before you try to get off. GRIFFIN (voice-over): But the newest billionaire won`t be the only one cashing in. More than 11 million tickets won something with cash prizes totaling $98 million including 3 more million dollar winners in the Golden State. The jackpot selling store`s owner Joseph Chahayed will also enjoy a million dollar bonus as we all wait for someone to claim that historic grand prize (on camera): What do you want to tell that person who is probably sitting at home trying to wrap his or her head? JOSEPH CHAHAYED, GAS STATION OWNER: I love you before and I love you know and I`m going to love you forever. (END VIDEOTAPE) GRIFFIN: So Papa Joe as he`s known around here is definitely filling that lottery love this morning. Now the winner has up to a year to claim that ticket. And if you weren`t the lucky winner, no worries. Guess what? There`s going to be another Powerball drawing tonight. Just a little smaller prize at $20 million, guys. MELVIN: All right, Dana Griffin, Dana, welcome to NBC News by the way. KOTB: Way to go, Dana. MELVIN: Welcome to the Peacock. KOTB: You did great report. GRIFFIN: Thank you. Thank you. Happy to be here. KOTB: All right. GUTHRIE: We won the lottery with her. MELVIN: There you go. Welcome to NBC. Let`s turn now to the latest on the new hurricane threat facing Florida this morning. KOTB: Yes, six weeks after and now Nicole taking aim at the state expected to gain strength before making landfall. We`re going to get to Dylan`s forecast in just a moment. But first, NBC`s Kerry Sanders he joins us from Daytona Beach shores. Hey, Kerry, good morning. KERRY SANDERS, NBC NEWS SENIOR NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Good morning guys. Look, you can see the Atlantic Ocean over my shoulder. It`s kicking up. The winds are picking up. The commercial airports in the area, that`s Orlando, Daytona Beach, Melbourne, they`re either closed or will be closing because of the approaching Tropical Storm that may become a Hurricane Nicole. [07:45:02] The big threat of course here is along the coast coastal erosion. And as you take a look at some of these pictures just leading into the arrival of Nicole, you`ll get a better understanding as to why Ian hammered this area and a lot of the coast was lost to the storm at the same time with the winds coming in. We have the threat to Artemis. OK. That rocket right now is sitting on the pad. It was supposed to launch on the 14th it`s now been pushed back to the 16th. It`s designed to withstand winds of about 85 miles per hour. But the real threat is going to be the rain. So NASA has put out staff to triple check all the hatches to make sure that everything is sealed. Meantime, mandatory evacuations from Flagler County all the way down to Martin County. Those who live in coastal Zone A have been told to leave. And as you saw from those pictures, the biggest threat of course with the coastal erosion is some of the buildings it`s feared by officials could actually have their foundations undermined and they could collapse. So a lot of attention anybody in a mobile home told also to go inland to shelters and then ultimately, tourists in the area who might be caught off guard, they should also find out where those shelters are. They`re open to everybody not just residents, guys. KOTB: Yes, good advice. Kerry Sanders for us there. Kerry, thank you. GUTHRIE: OK, let`s go to Dylan. She`s got the very latest on Nicole, the rest of today`s forecast in for Al this morning, hey. DREYER: Good morning again, guys. And I want to point out that hurricanes hitting the United States in November is pretty rare. We`ve only ever had it happen three times. So this would be the fourth one if this does strengthen into a category one storm. It is still a tropical storm, but it`s very close to being a weak category one so that`s why we do have your hurricane warnings in effect and it`s just north of West Palm Beach where we`re expecting landfall tonight, into tomorrow morning around 10:00 p.m. to about 2:00 a.m. tomorrow morning. And as this makes its way on shore, we are going to see that push of water. The good thing is it`s low tide when the storm is expected to make landfall but still on the backside of that your next high tide about six hours later, we could end up with a three to five foot storm surge. And we`re also looking for that to make its way up into the Northeast. Rainfall totals about eight inches possible in parts of Florida in the Northeast. We can see about two to four inches of rain. That`s a look at the weather across the country. Now here`s a peek out your window. (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that`s your latest forecast. [07:48:03] KOTB: All right, Dylan, thank you.
